entries.description:
Use this tool to create a structured task list for your current coding session. This helps you track progress, organize complex tasks, and demonstrate thoroughness to the user.
It also helps the user understand the progress of the task and overall progress of their requests.

## When to Use This Tool

Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:

- Complex multi-step tasks - When a task requires 3 or more distinct steps or actions
- Non-trivial and complex tasks - Tasks that require careful planning or multiple operations
- Plan mode - When using plan mode, create a task list to track the work
- User explicitly requests todo list - When the user directly asks you to use the todo list
- User provides multiple tasks - When users provide a list of things to be done (numbered or comma-separated)
- After receiving new instructions - Immediately capture user requirements as tasks
- When you start working on a task - Mark it as in_progress BEFORE beginning work
- After completing a task - Mark it as completed and add any new follow-up tasks discovered during implementation

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Skip using this tool when:
- There is only a single, straightforward task
- The task is trivial and tracking it provides no organizational benefit
- The task can be completed in less than 3 trivial steps
- The task is purely conversational or informational

NOTE that you should not use this tool if there is only one trivial task to do. In this case you are better off just doing the task directly.

## Task Fields

- **subject**: A brief, actionable title in imperative form (e.g., "Fix authentication bug in login flow")
- **description**: What needs to be done
- **activeForm** (optional): Present continuous form shown in the spinner when the task is in_progress (e.g., "Fixing authentication bug"). If omitted, the spinner shows the subject instead.

All tasks are created with status `pending`.

## Tips

- Create tasks with clear, specific subjects that describe the outcome
- After creating tasks, use TaskUpdate to set up dependencies (blocks/blockedBy) if needed
- Check TaskList first to avoid creating duplicate tasks

entries.description:
Use this tool to update a task in the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

**Mark tasks as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a task
- When a task is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned tasks as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call TaskList to find your next task

- ONLY mark a task as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the task as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new task describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a task as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete tasks:**
- When a task is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the task

**Update task details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between tasks

## Fields You Can Update

- **status**: The task status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the task title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the task description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the task owner (agent name)
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the task (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark tasks that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark tasks that must complete before this one can start

## Status Workflow

Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`

Use `deleted` to permanently remove a task.

## Staleness

Make sure to read a task's latest state using `TaskGet` before updating it.

## Examples

Mark task as in progress when starting work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "in_progress"}
```

Mark task as completed after finishing work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "completed"}
```

Delete a task:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "deleted"}
```

Claim a task by setting owner:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "owner": "my-name"}
```

Set up task dependencies:
```json
{"taskId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

# Rainbow screen kit (round 43) — one reusable process from a screen's OWN approved picture to a playable, measured 3D level

Generalises the proven Bubble Dash / Sock Rescue method (`tools/reflock`, 90.7 %, left untouched) so every playable screen (04–10) is built
the same way from its own approved artwork: real connected 3D geometry fitted to the picture, the picture's pixels baked onto that
geometry once (never projected live, no picture planes, no painted characters), the shared Benny + swipe controls + camera follow.
Free tools only (Blender 5.3 Geometry Nodes, three.js 0.180, OpenCV, onnxruntime); no credits.

## One command
```
bash tools/screenkit/get_models.sh                      # once per machine: free SAM 2.1 tiny + Depth Anything V2 small (Apache-2.0, ~255 MB)
bash tools/screenkit/setup_screen.sh 06 /tmp/ws06       # fit -> SAM 2 masks + clean plate -> Blender -> game folder (~10 s)
NODE_PATH=$(npm root -g) node tools/reflock/section_run.cjs /tmp/ws06/game /tmp/st06 stills 1.2 0 'sentinel=1'      # still at the picture camera
python3 -I tools/screenkit/compare_screen.py 06 /tmp/st06/s1.20_l0.png /tmp/ws06/seg/mask.png /tmp/cmp06 [--before F]   # measured likeness
TOUCH=1 NODE_PATH=$(npm root -g) node tools/reflock/section_run.cjs /tmp/ws06/game /tmp/run06 run end '<plan>' 'sentinel=1'   # whole level, real touch
python3 -I tools/reflock/encode_run.py /tmp/run06 <out> <name>                                                          # video + hole count
bash tools/screenkit/build_screen_app.sh 06 /tmp/ws06   # prebaked copy for the app -> public/screen06 (test route ?kit06=1 / VITE_RAINBOW_KIT06=1)
```

## Files
| file | what | screen-specific? |
|---|---|---|
| `fitlib.py` | camera from a vanishing point, ring-drift camera offset, ray / cylinder, centripetal Catmull-Rom through painted points | no |
| `screens/NN/fitNN.py` | the screen's OWN measurements -> `layout.json` (camera, drum, route, coins, paddles, bubbles, per-screen look values) | **yes (the only code per screen)** |
| `screens/NN/segmentNN.json` | SAM 2 prompts: HUD rows, title box, Benny box + points, swirl, coins, bubbles | **yes (data)** |
| `segment.py` | SAM 2.1 masks of what the game draws itself + OpenCV clean plate (`tools/reflock/plate.py`) | no |
| `blender_kit.py` | Geometry Nodes library: `RB_Sweep_Tube` (drums / tubes), `RB_Sweep_Ribbon` + `RB_Sweep_Flume` (banked river channel + its body), `RB_Sweep_Band` (gold rings), `RB_FoamBank` (scattered lumpy foam), plus pools and copper wall paddles; builds whatever `layout.json` lists, exports one GLB with clean UVs | no |
| `screen.html` | the game page: bake from N fitted cameras (depth-tested, masked, sharpness guard), code materials in the painting's style where no painted pixel is sharp enough, UV-flow water, Benny 31, `tools/kit05/controls.js` swipes, chase camera = the fitted picture camera kept in the route frame (exact at the picture position, smoothed in motion), QA API (`step`, `renderNow`, `camInfo`, `bennyBox`, `bennyVisBox`, `setBenny`, `routeCheck`, `sceneAudit`, `bakeStats`) | no |
| `setup_screen.sh`, `screen_export.cjs`, `build_screen_app.sh`, `compare_screen.py` | runnable folder, offline bake, app copy, measurement | no |
| `eval/` | the SAM 2 / Depth Anything controlled evaluation (`qa/reflock/r43/EXTRACTION_EVAL.md`) | no |

## Lessons paid for in round 43 (Blender 5.3 / three.js)
* Blender 5: Capture Attribute has a **Selection** socket at index 1 — link items BY NAME (`inputs['v']`), or the UVs become 0/1 booleans
  (every face spanned the whole texture; the bake then wrote one world point everywhere).
* Curve to Mesh: profile X -> the curve's right side, profile **Y -> down** (Z_UP twist): negate y when the profile is written as (across, up).
* A cyclic circle profile makes one face wrap backwards across the whole UV range: use an OPEN full arc (`GeometryNodeCurveArc`, 2π).
* Curve tilt +t lowers the right edge; the game's bank +b raises it (`tilt = -bank`).
* Blender 5: modifier inputs cannot be set as ID properties — set the node group's input defaults, then apply.
* Smoothing the route pulls it off the painted points (Benny drifted 50 px; the coins became uncollectable): Catmull-Rom THROUGH them.
* A painted crest above eye height can only show its TOP surface if it is banked toward the viewer (water-slide turn): the fit banks it.

## Screen 06 results (round 43) — `qa/reflock/r43/06/`
At the picture camera (412 × 915, compare_to_approved.py, scenery = picture minus HUD / Benny / swirl / coins / bubbles):
**89.5 % of scenery pixels within 20 levels**, SSIM 0.865, colour look 0.997 (previous game Screen 06: 3.6 %, SSIM 0.16).
----
{
 "dev": "vite --host 0.0.0.0",
 "build": "tsc --noEmit && vite build",
 "preview": "vite preview --host 0.0.0.0 --port 4173",
 "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit",
 "test:continuity": "vite-node scripts/continuity-test.ts",
 "models:export": "node scripts/export-models.mjs",
 "qa:capture": "node scripts/capture.mjs",
 "qa:compare": "python3 scripts/compare.py",
 "verify:refs": "sha256sum -c scripts/reference.sha256",
 "android:sync": "npm run build && npx cap sync android",
 "android:debug": "npm run android:sync && cd android && ./gradlew assembleDebug",
 "test:cinematic": "node scripts/cinematic-test.mjs"
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Rainbow screen kit: fetch the two FREE open models used by tools/screenkit (round 43 evaluation, qa/reflock/r43/EXTRACTION_EVAL.md):
#   SAM 2.1 hiera-tiny (Apache-2.0, ONNX export onnx-community/sam2.1-hiera-tiny-ONNX)   -> masks of Benny / coins in the approved pictures
#   Depth Anything V2 Small (Apache-2.0, onnx-community/depth-anything-v2-small)        -> optional depth cross-check (guide only)
# Runs with the already installed onnxruntime (no torch, no service, no credits). ~255 MB into $RAINBOW_MODELS (default ~/.cache/rainbow-models).
# Never committed to the repository (public repo, size).
set -e
M=${RAINBOW_MODELS:-$HOME/.cache/rainbow-models}; mkdir -p "$M/sam2" "$M/depth"
dl(){ [ -s "$2" ] && return 0; for i in 1 2 3 4; do curl -sSL --fail -o "$2.part" "$1" && mv "$2.part" "$2" && return 0; sleep $((i * 3)); done; echo "download failed: $1"; return 1; }
H=https://huggingface.co
for f in vision_encoder.onnx vision_encoder.onnx_data prompt_encoder_mask_decoder.onnx prompt_encoder_mask_decoder.onnx_data; do dl "$H/onnx-community/sam2.1-hiera-tiny-ONNX/resolve/main/onnx/$f" "$M/sam2/$f"; done
dl "$H/onnx-community/depth-anything-v2-small/resolve/main/onnx/model.onnx" "$M/depth/model.onnx"
python3 -c "import onnxruntime" 2>/dev/null || { echo "onnxruntime missing (pip install onnxruntime) - ask the user first"; exit 1; }
echo "models ready in $M"

  vs the painted SAM 2 silhouette (67,432)–(331,711) phone px.
* Per frame over the whole level (both runs): Benny's water point on the real water mesh (largest gap **0.001 u**, never without water under
  him), his up axis vs the surface normal ≤ 14.5° (incl. his lean into lane changes; route frame vs mesh ≤ 9°), immersion 11–18 % (median
  12.5 %) except during the leap (21 frames after the "up" swipe = out of the water, by design). Splash / wake / ripples are placed from his
  real water point and the real surface frame every step.

## 2. Plain-gray geometry test (`?gray=1&sentinel=1`: every surface gray + 0.5 u world grid, back faces orange, holes pure green)
Found and fixed: the pool faced DOWN; the pool and the channel were coplanar where the crest lands (z-fighting blotches) → pool faces up, 2 cm
under the channel (the channel rests IN the pool); the copper trays stood 2 cm off the drum wall (floating) → their straight edge is now 3 cm
INTO the wall. Then the whole level, real CDP touch (`GAMEPLAY_screen06_GRAY_geometry_real_touch.mp4`, `..._GRAY_contact_sheet.jpg`):
| check (585 frames) | result |
|---|---|
| hole pixels (green background) | **0** in all frames |
| Benny's whole body in the frame | 585 / 585 |
| real finger swipes detected | 14 / 14 (incl. a leap) |
| camera clearance from any scenery surface | ≥ 0.514 u (never inside / grazing a wall) |
| camera step / turn per frame | ≤ 0.094 u (forward travel 0.117) / ≤ 1.69° |
| scenery meshes that moved | 0 of 127 |
| channel bank followed | 0° → 71.6° on the crest → 0° |
Same-camera picture: `SCREEN06_4_GRAY_geometry_same_camera.jpg`.

## 3. Approved textures restored — same run, same swipes (`GAMEPLAY_screen06_TEXTURED_real_touch.mp4`, `..._TEXTURED_contact_sheet.jpg`)
Identical physical results (0 hole pixels in 585 frames, 585/585 on screen, 14/14 swipes, camera ≤ 1.69°/frame, water gap ≤ 0.001 u).
At the picture's camera position (compare_to_approved.py, unchanged 20-level threshold, scenery = picture minus HUD / Benny / swirl / coins / bubbles):
| | scenery px within 20 levels | SSIM | colour look |
|---|---|---|---|
| PREVIOUS game Screen 06 (`SCREEN06_2_PREVIOUS_old_game.jpg`) | 3.6 % | 0.16 | 0.10 |
| round 43 (Benny floating 4 % above the water) | 89.5 % | 0.865 | 0.997 |
| **NOW (Benny physically in the water)** (`SCREEN06_3_NEW_textured.jpg`) | **88.5 %** | 0.856 | 0.996 |
Tested and NOT kept (one factor at a time): 3D foam heaps placed by rays through the painted foam pixels (85.7 %: −2.8 points at the picture view
for a small gain in motion; available as `foam_from_picture`), coins at their exact painted 3D spots (88.5 %, no gain and not collectable on the
71° bank), texture LOD bias −0.4 / −1.2 (88.1 / 88.7 %; −0.8 kept for calm motion).
**In motion:** walls now in the measured painted magenta-pink (median 186/59/176) instead of lilac — moving-frame colour look 0.31–0.38
(round 43: 0.27–0.36); sharpness 0.91–1.11 of the painting except on the crest (0.54). Still below the start view: the close-up water is the
animated shader (cyan / pink bands, not the painted swirls), foam is far less than painted (1–5 % vs 9 %), and gold appears more later (rings).

## 4. Three.js DevTools MCP
Installed (plugin `parallax-threejs`) but its bridge only connects through its own dev-server proxy (port 9222 → 3000) in a browser tab; the
in-page QA hooks (`kitFrameQA`, `routeCheck`, ray probes, gray mode) answered every geometry / camera question this round, so it was not needed.

## 5. Not done
* 06 is not yet "the approved look while swimming" (colour look in motion ~0.3 vs 0.996 at the start) — next: the close-up water from the
  painted water, foam banks along the painted foam edges that do not cost the start view, the crest's 71° bank + camera roll for the user to judge.
* The app copy `public/screen06` is updated to this version; the APK in `qa/reflock/r43/` is still the round-43 build (rebuild at acceptance).

step_node() {
  local t v; t=$(now); v="$(node -v 2>/dev/null)"
  if [[ "$v" =~ ^v([0-9]+) ]] && [ "${BASH_REMATCH[1]}" -ge 20 ]; then rec node "Node.js" ok "$v, npm $(npm -v 2>/dev/null)" "$t"
  else rec node "Node.js" fail "need Node >= 20, found ${v:-none}" "$t"; fi
}

step_npm() {
  local t h=node_modules/.rainbow-bootstrap.sha256; t=$(now)
  if sha256sum --check --status "$h" 2>/dev/null && [ -d node_modules/three ] && [ -d node_modules/vite ]; then
    rec npm "npm dependencies" ok "node_modules up to date with package-lock.json (npm ci skipped)" "$t"; return
  fi
  if [ "$MODE" = check ]; then rec npm "npm dependencies" warn "node_modules missing or stale (run without --check)" "$t"; return; fi
  rm -f "$h"
  if timeout 900 npm ci --no-audit --no-fund --prefer-offline > "$LIVE/npm-ci.log" 2>&1; then
    sha256sum package.json package-lock.json > "$h"
    rec npm "npm dependencies" ok "npm ci done ($(ls node_modules | wc -l) packages; cache ~/.npm reused)" "$t"
  else rec npm "npm dependencies" fail "npm ci failed (backups/.live/npm-ci.log)" "$t"; fi
}

py_missing() { python3 -I -c 'import importlib.util as u,sys; print(" ".join(m for m in sys.argv[1:] if u.find_spec(m) is None))' "$@"; }

entries.description:
Resolves a package/product name to a Context7-compatible library ID and returns matching libraries.

You MUST call this function before 'Query Documentation' tool to obtain a valid Context7-compatible library ID UNLESS the user explicitly provides a library ID in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version' in their query.

Each result includes:
- Library ID: Context7-compatible identifier (format: /org/project)
- Name: Library or package name
- Description: Short summary
- Code Snippets: Number of available code examples
- Source Reputation: Authority indicator (High, Medium, Low, or Unknown)
- Benchmark Score: Quality indicator (100 is the highest score)
- Versions: List of versions if available. Use one of those versions if the user provides a version in their query. The format of the version is /org/project/version.

For best results, select libraries based on name match, source reputation, snippet coverage, benchmark score, and relevance to your use case.

Selection Process:
1. Analyze the query to understand what library/package the user is looking for
2. Return the most relevant match based on:
- Name similarity to the query (exact matches prioritized)
- Description relevance to the query's intent
- Documentation coverage (prioritize libraries with higher Code Snippet counts)
- Source reputation (consider libraries with High or Medium reputation more authoritative)
- Benchmark Score: Quality indicator (100 is the highest score)

Response Format:
- Return the selected library ID in a clearly marked section
- Provide a brief explanation for why this library was chosen
- If multiple good matches exist, acknowledge this but proceed with the most relevant one
- If no good matches exist, clearly state this and suggest query refinements

For ambiguous queries, request clarification before proceeding with a best-guess match.

IMPORTANT: Do not call this tool more than 3 times per question. If you cannot find what you need after 3 calls, use the best result you have.

libraryName.description: Library name to search for and retrieve a Context7-compatible library ID. Use the official library name with proper punctuation — e.g., 'Next.js' instead of 'nextjs', 'Customer.io' instead of 'customerio', 'Three.js' instead of 'threejs'.

query.description: What to look up in the library's documentation. This is used to rank library results by relevance to what the user is trying to accomplish. The query is sent to the Context7 API for processing. Do not include any sensitive or confidential information such as API keys, passwords, credentials, personal data, or proprietary code in your query.

#!/usr/bin/env sh
# macOS/Linux. Windows: use setup-spector.ps1 instead — POSIX shell
# doesn't run natively there. Both do the same thing; setup.ts picks the
# right one automatically based on platform.
#
# Clones and builds Spector.js's MCP server into a fixed, deterministic
# location so .mcp.json can reference it without a manual path edit.
set -e

PLUGIN_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
VENDOR_DIR="$PLUGIN_ROOT/vendor/spector"

if [ -d "$VENDOR_DIR" ]; then
  echo "Spector already vendored at $VENDOR_DIR — skipping clone."
else
  git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/BabylonJS/Spector.js.git "$VENDOR_DIR"
fi

cd "$VENDOR_DIR/mcp"
npm install
npm run build

echo "Spector MCP built at $VENDOR_DIR/mcp/dist/index.js"

content.content:
# Spector.js MCP Server

An MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that lets AI assistants debug **any WebGL website** using [Spector.js](https://spector.babylonjs.com/) — a WebGL debugger.

Load any URL, capture WebGL frames, and inspect draw calls, shaders, textures, and GL state — all from your AI-powered editor.

This server lives inside the Spector.js repository at `mcp/`.

## Architecture

```
AI Assistant ←→ MCP Server (stdio) ←→ Playwright (headless Chromium) ←→ Any WebGL Website + Spector.js
```

The server launches a headless browser, navigates to any URL, injects Spector.js at runtime, and exposes WebGL debugging capabilities as MCP tools.

When running from within the Spector.js repo, the server uses the locally built `dist/spector.bundle.js` from the repo root. This means you can test MCP tooling against local Spector.js changes without publishing. If the local bundle isn't found, it falls back to the npm-installed `spectorjs` package.

## Tools

### Navigation
| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `load_url` | Navigate to any URL and prepare for WebGL debugging. Works with any WebGL site. |
| `load_playground` | Convenience shortcut: load a Babylon.js Playground by snippet ID. Returns source code + screenshot. |
| `take_screenshot` | Screenshot the current canvas. |

### Canvas Selection
| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `list_canvases` | List all canvas elements on the page with WebGL context info. |
| `select_canvas` | Select which canvas to target when there are multiple on the page. |

### Capture & Inspection
| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `capture_frame` | Capture a single WebGL frame. Returns summary stats (commands, draw calls, programs, errors). |
| `get_draw_calls` | List all draw calls from the last capture with command IDs, names, and arguments. |
| `get_command_details` | Get full WebGL state at a specific command (blend, depth, stencil, bound textures, etc.). |
| `get_shaders` | Get shader program source code (vertex + fragment) with compile/link status. |
| `get_textures` | List texture uploads with dimensions, format, and type. |
| `get_webgl_state` | Compare initial vs final GL state for the frame — shows what changed. |

### Diagnostics
| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `get_context_info` | WebGL context details: version, extensions, capabilities, renderer. |
| `get_console_logs` | Browser console errors/warnings — catches JS errors and WebGL warnings. |

## Setup

### Prerequisites
- Node.js 18+

### Install

From the Spector.js repository root:

```bash
npm run mcp:install
npm run mcp:build
```

Or manually:

```bash
cd mcp
npm install
npx playwright install chromium
npm run build
```

### Configure MCP Client

Replace `<SPECTOR_REPO>` with the absolute path to your Spector.js repo clone.

**Claude Code / Copilot CLI** — add to your MCP settings:
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "spector": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["<SPECTOR_REPO>/mcp/dist/index.js"]
    }
  }
}
```

**VS Code (Copilot)** — add to `.vscode/mcp.json`:
```json
{
  "servers": {
    "spector": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["<SPECTOR_REPO>/mcp/dist/index.js"]
    }
  }
}
```

## Typical Workflows

### Debug any WebGL site
1. **Load a URL:**
   > "Load https://playground.babylonjs.com and capture a frame"

2. **Inspect rendering:**
   > "Show me the draw calls and shaders"
   > "Get the GL state at draw call #15"

### Debug a Babylon.js Playground
1. **Load by snippet:**
   > "Load playground #6FVG3Y and show me the code"

2. **Capture and analyze:**
   > "Capture a frame. Are there any GL errors?"

### Multi-canvas pages
1. **Discover canvases:**
   > "List the canvases on this page"

2. **Switch targets:**
   > "Select canvas #2 and capture a frame"

## Project Structure

```
mcp/
├── src/
│   ├── index.ts             # MCP server entry point with tool registrations
│   ├── browser-manager.ts   # BrowserManager class for Playwright browser lifecycle
│   ├── spector-bridge.ts    # Spector.js injection and frame capture
│   ├── capture-analyzer.ts  # Pure functions for analyzing capture data
│   ├── constants.ts         # Shared constants (timeouts, GL format maps)
│   ├── errors.ts            # Custom error hierarchy
│   └── types.ts             # Type definitions
├── dist/                    # Compiled output (generated by npm run build)
├── package.json
└── tsconfig.json
```

## Development

```bash
npm run dev     # Run with tsx (no build needed)
npm run build   # Build to dist/
npm start       # Run the built version
npm test        # Run unit tests
```

## Testing

```bash
npm test
```

Runs unit tests for the capture analyzer via Jest. Tests cover the pure analysis functions in `src/capture-analyzer.ts` (draw call extraction, shader parsing, texture enumeration, state diffing).

## Dependencies

- [@modelcontextprotocol/sdk](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk) — MCP server framework
- [Playwright](https://playwright.dev/) — headless browser automation
- [Spector.js](https://github.com/BabylonJS/Spector.js) — WebGL debugger (injected into the page at runtime)
- [Zod](https://zod.dev/) — schema validation

step_spector() {  # standalone official Spector.js MCP server (BabylonJS/Spector.js mcp/, free, MIT); user order 2026-11-22. The
  # parallax-threejs plugin's own Spector copy is never built in synced plugins, so this one is registered as "spectorjs" (user scope).
  local t d=$HOME/.local/share/rainbow-tools/Spector.js sha=755e6a7671e58424fcfda1270823a71e91de3553; t=$(now)
  if [ ! -f "$d/mcp/dist/index.js" ] && [ "$MODE" != check ]; then
    { rm -rf "$d" && mkdir -p "$d" && cd "$d" && git init -q && git remote add origin https://github.com/BabylonJS/Spector.js.git \
      && timeout 300 git fetch -q --depth 1 origin "$sha" && git checkout -q FETCH_HEAD && cd mcp \
      && timeout 600 npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund && npm run build && npm prune --omit=dev --no-audit --no-fund \
      && timeout 300 npm install --no-save --omit=dev --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund "playwright@$(node -p "require('playwright/package.json').version" 2>/dev/null || echo 1.63.0)"; \
    } > "$LIVE/spector-mcp.log" 2>&1; cd "$ROOT"
  fi
  if [ ! -f "$d/mcp/dist/index.js" ]; then rec spector "Spector.js MCP" warn "not built (backups/.live/spector-mcp.log)" "$t"; return; fi
  if command -v claude >/dev/null 2>&1 && ! claude mcp get spectorjs >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ "$MODE" != check ]; then
    claude mcp add spectorjs -s user -e PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers -- node "$d/mcp/dist/index.js" >> "$LIVE/spector-mcp.log" 2>&1
  fi
  if claude mcp get spectorjs >/dev/null 2>&1; then rec spector "Spector.js MCP" ok "spectorjs registered (BabylonJS/Spector.js @ ${sha:0:7}, playwright pinned to the preinstalled browser); tools load at session start" "$t"
  else rec spector "Spector.js MCP" warn "built but not registered (claude mcp add spectorjs ...)" "$t"; fi
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# RAINBOW — one-command recovery + environment bootstrap for a new Claude account or cloud session.
# Safe to run any number of times: every step checks first and only installs / merges what is missing.
#
#   bash scripts/claude-bootstrap.sh            full: resume newest work, LFS, refs, agents, Marble, tools, tests,
#                                               five-minute autosave, report (backups/BOOTSTRAP_REPORT.md)
#   bash scripts/claude-bootstrap.sh --check    report only: no installs, no merges (fetch is still done)
#   bash scripts/claude-bootstrap.sh --full     full + browser gameplay test + Screen 05 BEFORE pixel check
#                                               + fresh download of every LFS object from GitHub (SHA-256)
#   bash scripts/claude-bootstrap.sh --status   last report + autosave verdict (instant)
#   options: --no-tools (skip Blender/Android/pip/plugin installs)  --skip-resume (no merge; the DEFAULT since
#            2026-11-17)  --resume (merge newer ccr-*/claude/* branches — only with the user's explicit OK)
#   internal: --hook (SessionStart hook)  --background (rest of the hook run)  --env-setup (cloud setup script)
#
# New account, any start branch (the GitHub default branch is an OLD version):
#   git fetch origin <newest-branch> && git show FETCH_HEAD:scripts/claude-bootstrap.sh > /tmp/b.sh && bash /tmp/b.sh
#
# Safety: never force-pushes, resets, rebases, deletes files or rewrites history. Merges are normal merge commits;
# a merge that conflicts (outside auto-generated status files) is ABORTED and reported, never left half-done.
# Never pushes to backups/autosave.config.json -> protected_branches. Never reads, prints or stores credentials.
# Paid World Labs / Marble jobs are never started (only the free credit-balance read).

entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m -q --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

Spector.js is installed, connected, and has captured a real WebGL frame from Screen 06. Before I hand it over, I'm still checking that it reinstalls itself in future sessions.

**What I did**
- Downloaded the official server from github.com/BabylonJS/Spector.js. It sits in a tools folder outside your game repository and is pinned to one exact version of the code, so future installs match it.
- Spector ships a ready-made capture file, so only the small server needed building. Its development-only packages were removed afterwards.
- It needs a browser driver. I pinned it to the Chromium already installed here instead of downloading a second browser.
- Registered it in Claude Code as `spectorjs`. `claude mcp list` shows it as **✓ Connected**.

**Real test on Screen 06**, captured through Spector's own protocol, the same way Claude uses it:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Page loaded | "Rainbow 06", 1 WebGL2 canvas |
| One frame | 1,056 WebGL commands, 233 draw calls, 11 shader programs |
| GL errors | none |
| Screenshot | Screen 06 rendered correctly |

While Spector was attached, the browser console showed two Three.js messages ("context could not be created") and many "deleted object" warnings. They didn't appear when I opened the same page earlier without Spector, so they look like a side effect of Spector being attached. The frame rendered normally.

**Still to confirm:** to test the automatic reinstall, I removed my working install (a backup copy is kept) and started the normal session setup. It's still downloading branch information from GitHub; the Spector rebuild comes right after. If it fails, I'll restore the working copy.

**Two things to know**
- Spector's tools only appear in your next Claude session. This session started before it was installed, which is why I tested it through its own protocol.
- The old Spector entry inside the Three.js plugin will keep showing "failed to connect". It's left unbuilt and replaced by `spectorjs`, so you can ignore it.

Your branch, approved artwork and gameplay are unchanged, and no credits were used. There was nothing for you to approve.

The test script, capture results and screenshot are saved in `tools/spector/` and `qa/tools/spector_2026-11-22/`. They go to GitHub with the next autosave, along with the setup notes.

When the check finishes I'll confirm it here. Then, when you're ready: should I continue Screen 06 (the crest lean), and do you want the secure key form for your old World Labs key?

step_spector() {  # standalone official Spector.js MCP server (BabylonJS/Spector.js mcp/, free, MIT); user order 2026-11-22. The
  # parallax-threejs plugin's own Spector copy is never built in synced plugins, so this one is registered as "spectorjs" (user scope).
  local t d=$HOME/.local/share/rainbow-tools/Spector.js sha=755e6a7671e58424fcfda1270823a71e91de3553; t=$(now)
  if [ ! -f "$d/mcp/dist/index.js" ] && [ "$MODE" != check ]; then
    { rm -rf "$d" && mkdir -p "$d" && cd "$d" && git init -q && git remote add origin https://github.com/BabylonJS/Spector.js.git \
      && timeout 300 git fetch -q --depth 1 origin "$sha" && git checkout -q FETCH_HEAD && cd mcp \
      && timeout 600 npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund && npm run build && npm prune --omit=dev --no-audit --no-fund \
      && timeout 300 npm install --no-save --omit=dev --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund "playwright@$(node -p "require('playwright/package.json').version" 2>/dev/null || echo 1.63.0)"; \
    } > "$LIVE/spector-mcp.log" 2>&1; cd "$ROOT"
  fi
  if [ ! -f "$d/mcp/dist/index.js" ]; then rec spector "Spector.js MCP" warn "not built (backups/.live/spector-mcp.log)" "$t"; return; fi
  if command -v claude >/dev/null 2>&1 && ! claude mcp get spectorjs >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ "$MODE" != check ]; then
    claude mcp add spectorjs -s user -e PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers -- node "$d/mcp/dist/index.js" >> "$LIVE/spector-mcp.log" 2>&1
  fi
  if claude mcp get spectorjs >/dev/null 2>&1; then rec spector "Spector.js MCP" ok "spectorjs registered (BabylonJS/Spector.js @ ${sha:0:7}, playwright pinned to the preinstalled browser); tools load at session start" "$t"
  else rec spector "Spector.js MCP" warn "built but not registered (claude mcp add spectorjs ...)" "$t"; fi
}

+  fi

+  have=$(cd "$d/mcp" && node -p "require('./node_modules/playwright/package.json').version" 2>/dev/null)

+    (cd "$d/mcp" && timeout 300 npm install --no-save --omit=dev --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund "playwright@$pw") >> "$LIVE/spector-mcp.log" 2>&1

+  fi

# Screens 04–10: what the screen kit reuses and what each screen needs of its own (round 43, 2026-11-22)

Source: the user's approved pictures in `references/` (read-only), `analyze_reference.py` on each (`analysis_04_10/NN_analysis.json`,
`NN_overlay.jpg`), contact sheet in the round-43 report. Order of play (user, round 42): 04 → Bubble Dash → Sock Rescue → 05 → 06 → 07 → 08 → 09 → 10.
01, 02, 03 and 11 are the user's Google Flow videos and are never rebuilt.

## Kit components (tools/screenkit/blender_kit.py, Geometry Nodes) and where each picture uses them
| component | 04 | 05 | 06 | 07 | 08 | 09 | 10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| washer drum / tube (RB_Sweep_Tube, radius profile, segments) | warm-gold ring pipe | straight perforated tube | **built** (off-centre drum, 2.79 u) | tube with broad S-bends (bent axis) | chamber (wide, short) + far tube | room wall + porthole surround | room wall + porthole |
| gold rings (RB_Sweep_Band) | many warm-gold rings with bulbs | rings | **built** (broad bands) | rings with bulbs | one huge arch ring | porthole ring | porthole ring |
| river channel (RB_Sweep_Ribbon + Flume, banked) | slide into the pipe + **five arrows** | S-river | **built** (crest arch, banked to 72°) | S-river down the tube | S-river across the chamber | river + **big wave crest** (left) | river toward the towel |
| pool / floor water | — | pool | **built** | — | chamber floor water | yes | yes |
| foam banks (RB_FoamBank) | yes | yes | pool edges | yes | yes | yes + wave foam | yes |
| copper wall paddles (half-disc trays) | — | yes | **built** (2 painted) | yes | big trays + **waterfalls** | trays + waterfalls | trays |
| coins (painted trail, depth from painted size) | yes | yes | **built** | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| bubbles | yes | yes | **built** | yes | yes | yes | yes |

## Own geometry each screen still needs (new kit builders, same `grid()` / Geometry Nodes helpers)
* **04 Through the Five Arrows** — the laundry-room drain opening at the top (towel shelf, buttons), the warm-gold tunnel mouth, and the **five white
  chevron arrows** lying on the water (3D chevron slabs). Analysis: VP confidence LOW (the arrows hide the core) → confirm the VP by eye first.
* **05 Flow Into the Current** — already its own kit (`tools/kit05`, 80 % round 33); to move it onto the screen kit: tube + S-river + rings fit.
* **06 Crest the Rinse Arch** — DONE in round 43 (this kit): drum, crest channel, pool, rings, paddles.
* **07 Dive the Washer Tube** — tube with a bent axis (broad S-bends), ring bulbs; the 07 → 08 downward drop (path continuity).
* **08 Final Spin Chamber** — a chamber (not a tube): back wall with the **glass porthole door**, the **towel on a ledge**, side trays with
  **waterfalls**, the huge arch ring framing it; Benny box LOW confidence in the analysis (wide spray) → SAM 2 prompts needed.

# Reference-Locked 3D Scene Builder (round 40)

Real, connected 3D scenery built to match the user's approved pictures, played with the shared Benny + swipe controls, measured against the
pictures and tested IN MOTION. No forced perspective, no camera-relative depth curve, no live projection, no camera-facing scenery planes,
no screen overlays. Free tools only (Blender 5.3, three.js 0.180, OpenCV); no generation credits.

## Section 1: Bubble Dash Chamber -> golden arch -> Sock Rescue tunnel -> exit (`section.html`)
Pictures (read-only): `references/candidates/bonus_bubble_dash_chamber.webp`, `references/candidates/bonus_sock_rescue_laundry_tunnel.webp`.

| step | file | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| fit | `tools/bonus/fit_sock.py` + `fit_section.py` | camera of EACH picture fitted into ONE world (vanishing point, arch circle, water line, Benny; round-39 ring fit), scaled so the painted Benny has the same height in both; route = the painted river / coin trails; masks of what the game draws itself |
| geometry | `blender_section.py` (Blender headless) | 97 connected meshes with clean UVs -> `section.glb`: tunnel (arch sleeve, funnel, 2.5 u segments), gold rings, arch, bulkhead, side walls, back wall, ceiling, gold outlets + throats, waterfalls, pipes + collars, shirt tank + foam, lifter pods, towel rails + towels, socks |
| bake | `section.html` (at load, or offline for the app) | each picture is projected ONCE from its fitted camera into each mesh's own texture (depth-tested: only surfaces that camera really saw; masked HUD / Benny / coins; clean plates `plate.py` inside the masks at reduced weight); repeated furniture uses the best-seen instance as template |
| sharpness guard | `section.html` shaders | every baked texel stores how many picture pixels per metre it got; where it would be magnified on screen (> 1.3 phone px per picture px) the same-style code material takes over smoothly -> no blur close up, the painted look at the picture's distance |
| play | `section.html` + `tools/kit05/controls.js` + `swimfx.js` | Benny 31 (paddling / kick shader), swipes (lanes 0.3 u), leap / dive, 3D coins, socks mission, 3D foam domes + iridescent bubbles, flowing river shader, chase camera = the two fitted picture cameras relative to Benny, blended smoothly, following his lane |
| QA | `section_run.cjs`, `compare_section.py`, `app_route_check.cjs` | stills at the picture positions + skill `compare_to_approved.py`; full run with a swipe plan and per-frame checks (green-background hole count, Benny box on screen, camera step / turn per frame, static-world audit); in-app route check |
| app | `build_section_app.sh` + `src/game/bonusRoute.ts` | pre-baked section in `public/section/` (-> dist -> APK); the game hands over at the end of 04 and resumes at 05 (only with `VITE_RAINBOW_BONUS=1` / `?bonus=1`; default game unchanged) |

Rebuild: `bash tools/reflock/setup_section.sh <ws>` (fit + Blender + game folder, ~1 min) -> stills
`node tools/reflock/section_run.cjs <ws>/section <out> stills 0,20.204` -> measure
`MASK_BUBBLE=<ws>/section/mask_bubble.png python3 -I tools/reflock/compare_section.py <out>/s0.00_l0.png <out>/s20.20_l0.png <cmp>` ->
full run `node tools/reflock/section_run.cjs <ws>/section <run> run end '<plan json>' 'sentinel=1'` -> app `bash tools/reflock/build_section_app.sh <ws>`,
`VITE_RAINBOW_BONUS=1 npm run android:debug`.

## Reusing it for Screens 04 / 06 / 07 / 08 (after the user approves this section)
Generic and reused as is: the bake (any meshes, any number of fitted picture cameras), the sharpness guard, the masks / plates, Benny +
controls + camera blend, the QA harness and the app packaging. Per screen: a fit (its own measured features -> camera + layout JSON) and a
Blender layout script for its geometry family (ring tube: reuse `blender_section.py`'s tunnel / ring / pod builders; 06 crest, 08 chamber,
09 wave, 10 towel: new builders on the same `grid()` helper).

The earlier Screen-05 physical-tunnel test (`reflock.html`, `bake_phys.py`, `make_page.py`, `setup_reflock.sh`) used the locked Screen-05 picture;
the user then chose these two pictures instead.

def cmd_worldlabs() -> int:
    """Free, read-only Marble World API checks (no credits): balance + both pilot worlds. The key is injected by
    the Claude environment's proxy (network secret); this never reads, prints or stores it. Only an HTTP 401/403
    means the key must be reconnected — anything else (network, timeout, 5xx) is NOT a key problem."""
    api = "https://api.worldlabs.ai/marble/v1"
    man = json.loads((REPO / "backups" / "TOOL_MANIFEST.json").read_text())["marble_worldlabs"]

    def get(path: str):
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(api + path), timeout=25) as r:
                return r.status, json.loads(r.read() or b"{}")
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
            return e.code, {}
        except Exception as e:
            return None, {"error": str(e)[:100]}

    code, d = get("/credits")
    if code in (401, 403):
        return done("fail", f"Marble API authentication FAILED (HTTP {code}): reconnect with the secure credential form "
                            "(request_credential host api.worldlabs.ai, header WLT-Api-Key) - never chat or git")
    if code != 200:
        return done("warn", f"Marble API not reachable (HTTP {code or d.get('error')}): network/API problem, NOT a key "
                            "problem - do not ask the user for a new key; retry later")
    worlds = []
    for w in man["worlds"]:
        c, _ = get(f"/worlds/{w['world_id']}")
        worlds.append(f"{w['label']} {c}")
    bad = [x for x in worlds if not x.endswith(" 200")]
    status = "warn" if bad else "ok"
    return done(status, f"Marble API key authenticated (free read: {d.get('remaining_credits', '?'):.0f} credits); worlds "
                        f"{', '.join(worlds)}; no paid job started")

"""Round 44: join sheet + numbers from tools/world/join_audit.cjs captures.
For every join of the route (04 -> A -> B -> 05 -> 06 -> 07 -> 08 -> 09 -> 10): EXIT frames | ENTRANCE frames side by side, and the measured
change across the join between the last exit frame and the first entrance frame (HUD band excluded):
  * colour jump: CIE76 delta-E of the mean Lab colour of the scenery band (y 12-55 % of the frame) and of the water band (y 60-100 %)
  * page load: whether the app reloads a page there today (a hard cut + loading screen)
python3 -I tools/world/join_sheet.py <captures dir> <out.jpg> <out.json>"""
import json
import sys

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw

cap, out_jpg, out_json = sys.argv[1:4]
JOINS = [  # (label, exit frames, entrance frames, page load today)
    ('04 -> A  Bubble Dash', ['J1_04_exit_a', 'J1_04_exit_b'], ['J1_A_entrance_a', 'J1_A_entrance_b'], True),
    ('A -> B  Sock Rescue', ['J2_A_exit_b'], ['J2_B_entrance_a'], False),
    ('B -> 05', ['J3_B_exit_a', 'J3_B_exit_b'], ['J3_05_entrance_a', 'J3_05_entrance_b'], True),
    ('05 -> 06 (rebuilt 06)', ['J4_05_exit_a', 'J4_05_exit_b'], ['K6_kit06_entrance_picture'], True),
    ('06 (rebuilt) -> 07', ['K6_kit06_exit_a', 'K6_kit06_exit_b'], ['J5_07_entrance_a', 'J5_07_entrance_b'], True),
    ('07 -> 08', ['J6_07_exit_a', 'J6_07_exit_b'], ['J6_08_entrance_a', 'J6_08_entrance_b'], False),
    ('08 -> 09', ['J7_08_exit_a', 'J7_08_exit_b'], ['J7_09_entrance_a', 'J7_09_entrance_b'], False),
    ('09 -> 10', ['J8_09_exit_a', 'J8_09_exit_b'], ['J8_10_entrance_a', 'J8_10_entrance_b'], False),
]


def lab(a):
    a = a / 255.0
    a = np.where(a > 0.04045, ((a + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4, a / 12.92)
    xyz = a @ np.array([[0.4124, 0.2126, 0.0193], [0.3576, 0.7152, 0.1192], [0.1805, 0.0722, 0.9505]])
    xyz = xyz / np.array([0.9505, 1.0, 1.089])
    f = np.where(xyz > 0.008856, np.cbrt(xyz), 7.787 * xyz + 16 / 116)
    return np.stack([116 * f[..., 1] - 16, 500 * (f[..., 0] - f[..., 1]), 200 * (f[..., 1] - f[..., 2])], -1)


def bands(name):
    im = np.asarray(Image.open(f'{cap}/{name}.png').convert('RGB'), dtype=np.float64)
    h = im.shape[0]
    L = lab(im)
    return L[int(0.12 * h):int(0.55 * h)].reshape(-1, 3).mean(0), L[int(0.60 * h):].reshape(-1, 3).mean(0)


W, H, LBL = 160, 356, 34
rows = []
sheet = Image.new('RGB', (W * 4 + 230, len(JOINS) * (H + LBL)), (24, 10, 36))
d = ImageDraw.Draw(sheet)
for r, (label, ex, en, pl) in enumerate(JOINS):
    y = r * (H + LBL)
    s0, w0 = bands(ex[-1]); s1, w1 = bands(en[0])
    dE_s, dE_w = float(np.linalg.norm(s0 - s1)), float(np.linalg.norm(w0 - w1))
    rows.append({'join': label, 'page_load_today': pl, 'colour_jump_scenery_dE': round(dE_s, 1), 'colour_jump_water_dE': round(dE_w, 1),
                 'exit_frames': ex, 'entrance_frames': en})
    frames = (ex + [None] * (2 - len(ex)))[:2] + (en + [None] * (2 - len(en)))[:2]
    for i, n in enumerate(frames):
        x = 230 + i * W
        if n:
            sheet.paste(Image.open(f'{cap}/{n}.png').convert('RGB').resize((W, H)), (x, y + LBL))
        d.text((x + 3, y + 4), ('EXIT' if i < 2 else 'ENTRANCE') + (f'  {n.split("_", 1)[1]}' if n else ''), fill=(255, 255, 255))
    d.line([(230 + 2 * W - 1, y + LBL), (230 + 2 * W - 1, y + LBL + H)], fill=(255, 230, 80), width=3)
    d.text((8, y + 40), label, fill=(255, 230, 120))
    d.text((8, y + 70), ('PAGE LOAD today (hard cut)' if pl else 'same scene today'), fill=(255, 120, 120) if pl else (140, 230, 140))
    d.text((8, y + 100), f'colour jump scenery dE {dE_s:.1f}', fill=(230, 230, 230))
    d.text((8, y + 120), f'colour jump water   dE {dE_w:.1f}', fill=(230, 230, 230))
sheet.save(out_jpg, quality=86)
json.dump({'joins': rows, 'note': 'dE = CIE76 difference of the mean Lab colour across the join (last exit frame vs first entrance frame); '
           'about 2 is barely visible, above 10 is an obvious change'}, open(out_json, 'w'), indent=1)
for row in rows:
    print(f"{row['join']:24s} page load {str(row['page_load_today']):5s}  scenery dE {row['colour_jump_scenery_dE']:5.1f}  water dE {row['colour_jump_water_dE']:5.1f}")

change across the join between the last exit frame and the first entrance frame (HUD band excluded):
  * colour jump: CIE76 delta-E of the mean Lab colour of the scenery band (y 12-55 % of the frame) and of the water band (y 60-100 %)
  * page load: whether the app reloads a page there today (a hard cut + loading screen)
python3 -I tools/world/join_sheet.py <captures dir> <out.jpg> <out.json>"""
import json
import sys

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw

cap, out_jpg, out_json = sys.argv[1:4]
JOINS = [  # (label, exit frames, entrance frames, page load today)
    ('04 -> A  Bubble Dash', ['J1_04_exit_a', 'J1_04_exit_b'], ['J1_A_entrance_a', 'J1_A_entrance_b'], True),
    ('A -> B  Sock Rescue', ['J2_A_exit_b'], ['J2_B_entrance_a'], False),
    ('B -> 05', ['J3_B_exit_a', 'J3_B_exit_b'], ['J3_05_entrance_a', 'J3_05_entrance_b'], True),
    ('05 -> 06 (rebuilt 06)', ['J4_05_exit_a', 'J4_05_exit_b'], ['K6_kit06_entrance_picture'], True),
    ('06 (rebuilt) -> 07', ['K6_kit06_exit_a', 'K6_kit06_exit_b'], ['J5_07_entrance_a', 'J5_07_entrance_b'], True),
    ('07 -> 08', ['J6_07_exit_a', 'J6_07_exit_b'], ['J6_08_entrance_a', 'J6_08_entrance_b'], False),
    ('08 -> 09', ['J7_08_exit_a', 'J7_08_exit_b'], ['J7_09_entrance_a', 'J7_09_entrance_b'], False),
    ('09 -> 10', ['J8_09_exit_a', 'J8_09_exit_b'], ['J8_10_entrance_a', 'J8_10_entrance_b'], False),
]


def lab(a):
    a = a / 255.0
    a = np.where(a > 0.04045, ((a + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4, a / 12.92)
    xyz = a @ np.array([[0.4124, 0.2126, 0.0193], [0.3576, 0.7152, 0.1192], [0.1805, 0.0722, 0.9505]])
    xyz = xyz / np.array([0.9505, 1.0, 1.089])
    f = np.where(xyz > 0.008856, np.cbrt(xyz), 7.787 * xyz + 16 / 116)
    return np.stack([116 * f[..., 1] - 16, 500 * (f[..., 0] - f[..., 1]), 200 * (f[..., 1] - f[..., 2])], -1)

## 1. Where the joins are today (BEFORE) — `qa/world/r44/join_audit_BEFORE/`
Built app (`dist/` = the APK's files, `VITE_RAINBOW_BONUS=1 VITE_RAINBOW_KIT06=1`), 412 × 915, 2 frames before + 2 after every join

|---|---|---|---|

| 06 (rebuilt) → 07 | **page load (hard cut)** | 30.8 / 11.4 | rebuilt 06 drum end → old 07 tube |
| 07 → 08 | same scene (old game) | 19.3 / 6.4 | continuous 61 u plunge; the 08 porthole is already visible from 07 |
| 08 → 09 | same scene | 1.6 / 7.0 | same chamber |
| 09 → 10 | same scene | 8.1 / 8.2 | same chamber |

Units differ between the three engines (Benny ≈ 0.47 u in the section, 0.57 u in the kit 06, ≈ 1.6–2 u in the old game; tube radius / Benny:
sock tube 2.1, 04 pipe ≈ 2.7, 05 ≈ 4.2, 06 drum 4.9, 07 ≈ 4) — every connector has to change the tunnel size gradually, and Benny must be
the same size on screen across each join.

**(Recommended) One world built with the screen kit.** A world container loads the areas in route order and places each one so its
entrance sits exactly on the previous exit (position, direction, water level, tunnel size); one route, one Benny, one camera, one set of swipe
controls, no page loads. Short Blender Geometry-Nodes connectors are built between areas from the preview's captions (04's arrow pipe opening
into the Bubble Dash chamber; the sock tunnel curving and widening into the 05 current; the 06 crest dropping into the 07 tube; the 07 tube
opening into the 08 spin chamber), coloured as a blend of the two areas' measured palettes. Areas: A + B (built, 90.7 %) and 06 (built,
88.5 %) as they are; 04, 05, 07, 08, 09, 10 rebuilt with the kit from their own approved pictures (baked pixels on real geometry — the method
the user's rules require; several old-game screens still use camera projection), in this order: 04 + 05 (for 04 → A → B → 05), then 07 + 08
(for 07 → 08), then 09, 10. The app switches to the world when it is complete; until then the current game stays unchanged.
**Alternative (faster, partial): splice A + B and the rebuilt 06 into the current game.** Removes the page loads sooner, but keeps the older
04 / 05 / 07–10 (built with methods since ruled out) and would be redone when those screens are rebuilt.

## 3. Rules for every join (checked by `join_audit.cjs` on the world, AFTER vs BEFORE)
No page load / scene swap; the water surface continuous (no gap, no step) and flowing the same way; tunnel size changing gradually; no
repeated entrances (each opening seen once); camera without jumps (step / turn per frame limits as in the kit runs); Benny the same size on
screen across the join; colour jump across each join small (target dE < 10) while each area keeps its own measured likeness.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Rainbow screen kit: one command from a screen's approved picture to a runnable, measured 3D level folder (round 43).
#   bash tools/screenkit/setup_screen.sh <NN> <workspace> [asset_repo=/home/user/rainbow-]
# 1. fit      : tools/screenkit/screens/NN/fitNN.py -> layout.json + overlays (optional Depth Anything cross-check if its depth file exists)
# 2. masks    : tools/screenkit/segment.py (SAM 2.1 traced Benny / coins, clean plate) from screens/NN/segmentNN.json
# 3. geometry : Blender 5.3 headless, tools/screenkit/blender_kit.py (Geometry Nodes components) -> scene.glb
# 4. game     : tools/screenkit/screen.html + the shared game code (controls.js, swimfx.js, Benny 31, three.js 0.180)
# Free: no generation service, no credits. The approved picture is only READ (copied into the game folder for the bake).
set -e
NN=${1:?screen number}; SRC=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd); WS=${2:?workspace}; AR=${3:-/home/user/rainbow-}
mkdir -p "$WS/fit" "$WS/seg" "$WS/game"; WS=$(cd "$WS" && pwd); G="$WS/game"; SD="$SRC/tools/screenkit/screens/$NN"
REF=$(python3 -c "import json,sys;print(json.load(open('$SRC/.claude/skills/rainbow-screen-builder/screens.json'))['screens']['$NN']['reference'])")
DA2=""; M=${RAINBOW_MODELS:-$HOME/.cache/rainbow-models}
if [ -f "$M/depth/model.onnx" ] && [ ! -f "$WS/fit/da2.npy" ]; then
  (cd "$SRC" && python3 -I - "$REF" "$WS/fit/da2.npy" "$M" <<'EOF' >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
import sys, os, numpy as np
from PIL import Image
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.getcwd(), 'tools', 'screenkit', 'eval'))
from eval_extract import Depth
d = Depth(os.path.join(sys.argv[3], 'depth')); np.save(sys.argv[2], d(np.asarray(Image.open(sys.argv[1]).convert('RGB'))).astype(np.float16))
EOF
  )
fi
[ -f "$WS/fit/da2.npy" ] && DA2="--da2 $WS/fit/da2.npy"
(cd "$SRC" && python3 -I "$SD/fit$NN.py" "$WS/fit" $DA2 > "$WS/fit/fit.log")
(cd "$SRC" && python3 -I tools/screenkit/segment.py "$REF" "$SD/segment$NN.json" "$WS/seg" > "$WS/seg/segment.log")
blender -b --python "$SRC/tools/screenkit/blender_kit.py" -- "$WS/fit/layout.json" "$G/scene.glb" > "$WS/fit/blender.log" 2>&1 || { tail -20 "$WS/fit/blender.log"; exit 1; }
python3 - "$WS/fit/layout.json" "$G/layout.json" <<'EOF'
import json, sys
L = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
for i, c in enumerate(L['cams']): c['plate'] = f'plate_{i}.png'; c['mask'] = f'mask_{i}.png'
json.dump(L, open(sys.argv[2], 'w'))
EOF
cp -f "$WS/seg/plate.png" "$G/plate_0.png"; cp -f "$WS/seg/mask.png" "$G/mask_0.png"; cp -f "$SRC/$REF" "$G/ref_0.png"
cp -f "$SRC/tools/screenkit/screen.html" "$G/play3.html"; cp -f "$SRC/tools/kit05/controls.js" "$SRC/tools/kit05/swimfx.js" "$G/"
cp -fL "$AR/assets/models/benny31.glb" "$G/benny31.glb"; cp -fL "$AR/assets/textures/benny31/bake.png" "$G/bake.png"; cp -fL "$AR/assets/textures/paint/05_coin.png" "$G/coin.png"
for f in splash.png bubble.png glint.png; do cp -fL "$AR/tools/marble05/viewer/$f" "$G/$f"; done
if [ ! -d /tmp/rainbow_r34/node_modules/three ]; then (mkdir -p /tmp/rainbow_r34 && cd /tmp/rainbow_r34 && npm init -y >/dev/null && npm install three@0.180.0 >/dev/null 2>&1); fi
ln -sfn /tmp/rainbow_r34/node_modules "$G/node_modules"
head -c 200 "$G/benny31.glb" | grep -q "git-lfs" && { echo "SETUP FAILED: benny31.glb is an LFS pointer"; exit 1; }
head -2 "$WS/fit/fit.log"; cat "$WS/seg/segment.log"; tail -1 "$WS/fit/blender.log" | head -1; echo "screen $NN ready: $G/play3.html"

"""Screen 06 'Crest the Rinse Arch' - FIT step of the screen kit (round 43). Measures the user's approved picture
references/06_crest_the_rinse_arch.png (read-only) and writes ONE physical world for it: <out>/layout.json (components for
tools/screenkit/blender_kit.py, the fitted picture camera, Benny, coins, route) + fit overlays.
  python3 -I tools/screenkit/screens/06/fit06.py <out dir> [--da2 <inverse depth .npy of the picture (optional guide)>]

Measured on the picture (864 x 1536 px; every number re-checkable on the gridded crops in qa/reflock/r43/06/measure/):
  * drum axis vanishing point (700, 605): where the RANSAC-fitted gold ring circles converge (centres (600,520) r 260, (652,586) r 167,
    (674,593) r 76); their centres drift toward the VP with shrinking radius -> camera offset from the drum axis (fitlib.ring_offsets).
  * Benny: water contact under his body (425, 1175), pompom top (418, 735); the camera is CAM_H above the water there.
  * the coin trail on the crest (analyze_reference.py coins, radii 46 -> 8.6 px): coins are equal in size, so each coin's painted
    radius gives its depth (depth = k / radius); k from the first coin, which floats on the water just ahead of Benny's lane.
  * the crest ribbon = a smooth curve through Benny's water point and the coin points (coin centre lowered to the water), rising up
    to the left (the arch), turning right over the crest and descending into the drum toward the vanishing point, then continuing on
    the drum floor (Screen 07 takes over there).
  * drum radius: the painted drum wall must enclose the crest with a margin and pass the paddles; see DRUM_R below.
Optional guide (adopted only as a guide, round 43 evaluation): Depth Anything V2's inverse depth of the picture, calibrated on the
floor water (exact depth from the water plane), is printed next to the coin depths as a cross-check; it never sets geometry.
"""
import sys, os, json, math, argparse
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)); KIT = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(HERE, '..', '..')); REPO = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(KIT, '..', '..'))
sys.path.insert(0, KIT)
import fitlib as fl   # noqa: E402

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(); ap.add_argument('out'); ap.add_argument('--da2'); a = ap.parse_args(); os.makedirs(a.out, exist_ok=True)
REF = 'references/06_crest_the_rinse_arch.png'; W, H = 864, 1536
M = dict(vp=(700.0, 605.0), rings=[(600.0, 520.0, 260.0), (652.0, 586.0, 167.0), (674.0, 593.0, 76.0)],
         benny_water=(425.0, 1175.0), benny_top=(418.0, 735.0),
         coins=[(267.5, 716.7, 46.0), (178.9, 623.6, 37.1), (234.3, 547.8, 26.5), (320.3, 520.7, 18.8), (407.7, 533.3, 14.0), (506.0, 585.2, 10.0),
                (557.3, 621.7, 9.0), (594.9, 643.4, 9.0), (619.2, 654.2, 8.6)],
         paddles=[(285.0, 240.0, 150.0), (155.0, 398.0, 165.0)],          # painted tray centre x, y and painted width (px)
         bubbles=[(70, 742, 34), (233, 380, 16), (262, 465, 18), (108, 478, 18), (88, 1452, 38), (695, 1352, 38), (205, 862, 26), (365, 645, 20), (434, 505, 15),
                  (790, 890, 14), (693, 1218, 24), (520, 566, 12), (10, 950, 30), (45, 1185, 16)])
cam = fl.Cam(W, H)
yaw, pitch = fl.yaw_pitch_from_vp(cam, M['vp'])
cam.set(yaw, pitch, [0.0, fl.CAM_H, 0.0])
# ---- Benny: his water point and painted height (pompom top above the water)
Pb = cam.on_plane_y(*M['benny_water']); dtop = cam.ray(*M['benny_top']); lam = (Pb[2] - cam.C[2]) / dtop[2]; HB = float((cam.C + lam * dtop)[1])
# ---- coins: equal real size -> depth from the painted radius. The first coin floats on the water (its lowest point on y = 0).
def coin_at(px, py, r, k):
    d = cam.depth_dir(px, py); return cam.C + d * (k / r)
COIN_D_PER_BENNY = 0.477        # coin diameter / Benny height in the proven Bubble Dash fit (section.json): same coins, same Benny
COIN_R = 0.5 * COIN_D_PER_BENNY * HB; k = COIN_R * cam.F     # camera-space depth of a coin = k / painted radius
# depth from the painted size; tiny far coins (radius < 12 px: +-1 px = +-10 %) must keep receding along the trail (>= 1.2 u apart)
deps = [k / r for _, _, r in M['coins']]
for i in range(1, len(deps)):
    if M['coins'][i][2] < 12: deps[i] = max(deps[i], deps[i - 1] + 1.2)
coins = [cam.C + cam.depth_dir(x, y) * dz for (x, y, _), dz in zip(M['coins'], deps)]
water_pts = [P - np.array([0, COIN_R, 0]) for P in coins]                                  # the river surface under each coin
# ---- optional Depth Anything V2 cross-check (guide only): calibrate on floor water pixels, print its depth at the coins
da2_check = None
if a.da2 and os.path.exists(a.da2):
    D = np.load(a.da2).astype(np.float64); ys = np.arange(1250, 1500, 25); xs = np.arange(120, 760, 40); A_, b_ = [], []
    for y in ys:
        for x in xs:
            P = cam.on_plane_y(x, y); z = float(-(cam.R.T @ (P - cam.C))[2]); A_.append([D[y, x], 1.0]); b_.append(1.0 / z)
    s_, t_ = np.linalg.lstsq(np.array(A_), np.array(b_), rcond=None)[0]
    da2_check = [{'coin': i, 'depth_from_size': round(float(k / r), 3), 'depth_da2': round(float(1.0 / max(1e-4, s_ * np.median(D[int(y) - 2:int(y) + 3, int(x) - 2:int(x) + 3]) + t_)), 3)}
                 for i, (x, y, r) in enumerate(M['coins'])]

rem=pts.copy(); found=[]

    if best is None: break

    found.append((int(inl.sum()),round(cx,1),round(cy,1),round(r,1),cov)); rem=rem[~inl]

def grid(name, nu, nv, fn, flip=False):
    """plain parametric grid (as tools/reflock/blender_section.py): fn(a, b) -> (game xyz, (u, v))"""
    me = bpy.data.meshes.new(name); bm = bmesh.new(); uvl = bm.loops.layers.uv.new('UVMap'); V, UV = [], []
    for j in range(nv + 1):
        row, ru = [], []
        for i in range(nu + 1):
            p, uv = fn(i / nu, j / nv); row.append(bm.verts.new(B2(p))); ru.append(uv)
        V.append(row); UV.append(ru)
    for j in range(nv):
        for i in range(nu):
            q = [V[j][i], V[j][i + 1], V[j + 1][i + 1], V[j + 1][i]]; uq = [UV[j][i], UV[j][i + 1], UV[j + 1][i + 1], UV[j + 1][i]]
            if flip: q, uq = q[::-1], uq[::-1]
            f = bm.faces.new(q)
            for l, uv in zip(f.loops, uq): l[uvl].uv = uv
    bm.to_mesh(me); bm.free(); ob = bpy.data.objects.new(name, me); bpy.context.collection.objects.link(ob)
    for p in me.polygons: p.use_smooth = True
    return ob


def tube_segments(prefix, axis_pts, radius, seg_len, res=96):
    """washer drum / tube: the axis polyline split into segments of seg_len (each its own 0..1 UVs for the bake), RB_Sweep_Tube"""
    ng = sweep_group('RB_Sweep_Tube', prof_circle(res), flip=True)
    L = [0.0]
    for i in range(1, len(axis_pts)): L.append(L[-1] + math.dist(axis_pts[i], axis_pts[i - 1]))
    n = max(1, round(L[-1] / seg_len)); out = []
    for k in range(n):
        a, b = L[-1] * k / n, L[-1] * (k + 1) / n; pts = []
        for j in range(9):
            t = a + (b - a) * j / 8; i = max(1, min(len(L) - 1, next((m for m in range(1, len(L)) if L[m] >= t), len(L) - 1))); f = (t - L[i - 1]) / max(1e-9, L[i] - L[i - 1])
            pts.append([axis_pts[i - 1][c] + (axis_pts[i][c] - axis_pts[i - 1][c]) * f for c in range(3)])
        ob = curve_object(f'{prefix}_{k:02d}', pts, [radius(p) for p in pts]); out.append(apply_group(ob, ng))
    return out


def ribbon(prefix, route, bank, width, seg_len, flume=True):
    """water channel along the route: the ribbon surface (water_*) and, under it, the flume body (flume_*), both banked by `bank`"""
    rib = object_profile_group('RB_Sweep_Ribbon', [(-1.0, 0.0), (-0.5, 0.0), (0.0, 0.0), (0.5, 0.0), (1.0, 0.0)])
    flu = object_profile_group('RB_Sweep_Flume', [(-1.0, 0.0), (-1.07, -0.02), (-1.12, -0.09), (-1.1, -0.18), (-1.0, -0.24), (-0.6, -0.27), (0.0, -0.28),
                                                   (0.6, -0.27), (1.0, -0.24), (1.1, -0.18), (1.12, -0.09), (1.07, -0.02), (1.0, 0.0)], flip=True)
    L = [0.0]
    for i in range(1, len(route)): L.append(L[-1] + math.dist(route[i], route[i - 1]))
    n = max(1, round(L[-1] / seg_len)); per = (len(route) - 1) / n; out = []
    for k in range(n):
        i0, i1 = round(k * per), round((k + 1) * per); pts = route[i0:i1 + 1]; tl = [-b for b in bank[i0:i1 + 1]]
        out.append(apply_group(curve_object(f'{prefix}_{k:02d}', pts, [width / 2] * len(pts), tl), rib))
        if flume: out.append(apply_group(curve_object(f'flume_{prefix}_{k:02d}', pts, [width / 2] * len(pts), tl), flu))
    return out


def foam_bank(name, pts, spacing, size, seed):
    ng = foam_group(); ob = curve_object(name, pts); return apply_group(ob, ng, {'Spacing': spacing, 'Size': size, 'Seed': seed})


def paddle(name, pos, axis_pt, width):
    """copper half-disc tray standing out of the drum wall (the painted trays of 05 / 06 / 07): its straight edge lies in the wall"""
    c = Vector(pos); a = Vector((axis_pt[0], axis_pt[1], pos[2])); inward = (a - c).normalized(); along = Vector((0, 0, -1.0)); side = inward.cross(along).normalized()
    R = width / 2; T = 0.11 * width
    def f(u, v):
        th = math.pi * u                                    # half disc: along the tube from -R to +R, out of the wall up to R
        if v < 0.25: k = v / 0.25; rr = R * k; h = T / 2           # top face
        elif v < 0.75: k = (v - 0.25) / 0.5; rr = R; h = T / 2 - T * k   # rim band
        else: k = (v - 0.75) / 0.25; rr = R * (1 - k); h = -T / 2        # underside
        p = c + along * (rr * math.cos(th)) + inward * (rr * math.sin(th) - 0.03) + side * h   # r43b gray test: straight edge 3 cm INTO the wall (was 2 cm off it = floating)
        return ((p.x, p.y, p.z), (u, v))
    return grid(name, 48, 24, f)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- the screen
D = LAY['drum']; xa, ya, R = D['axis_x'], D['axis_y'], D['r']
zf = D.get('z_far', D['z1'])
tube_segments('tunnel', [[xa, ya, D['z0']], [xa, ya, zf]], lambda p: R, D.get('seg', 2.5))
if zf > D['z1'] + 1e-6: tube_segments('tunnelfar', [[xa, ya, zf], [xa, ya, D['z1']]], lambda p: R, D.get('seg_far', 12.0), res=72)   # the far drum: longer segments
z_r = [z for z in LAY['rings']['z'] if D['z1'] < z < D['z0']]
zz = (min(z_r) if z_r else D['z0'] - 6) - LAY['rings']['spacing']
while zz > D['z1'] + 1: z_r.append(zz); zz -= LAY['rings']['spacing']
bw = LAY['rings']['band']
for i, z in enumerate(sorted(z_r, reverse=True)):
    # band ring: unit profile scaled by the curve radius (= band width), centred on the wall circle slightly inside the drum
    prof_scale = bw
    pts = [[xa + (R - 0.04) * math.cos(2 * math.pi * j / 160), ya + (R - 0.04) * math.sin(2 * math.pi * j / 160), z] for j in range(161)]

Claudia, I want to clarify exactly how I want you to build my Rainbow game's connected 3D scenery.

Please use Blender 5.3 and Geometry Nodes as the primary tools for building the actual playable environments.

I want my approved screens reconstructed as real, complete, connected 3D worlds—not flat images or backgrounds that only look correct from one camera position.

1. Use Blender for the real scenery

Build the actual geometry for:

- Washer tunnels and metallic drum walls
- Golden rings and washing-machine machinery
- Curved rainbow water channels and slides
- Foam banks, obstacles and physical boundaries
- Entrances, exits and transitions between levels
- Collision surfaces that correspond to what players see

Use my approved images as the visual blueprints. Preserve the original scenery designs and colors.

2. World Labs Atlas is optional, not the main builder

You may evaluate World Labs Atlas for specific 3D assets or scenery details when it would meaningfully improve accuracy or construction speed.

However, do not replace our existing Blender-built playable environments with generated splat scenes.

If you propose using Atlas, first explain the specific task, expected benefit, output format and credit cost. Get my approval before any paid generation.

If using a generated asset, verify its geometry, textures and collisions and integrate it into the existing Blender/Three.js world.

Don't use my old, rejected Marble world reconstructions.

3. Use Three.js for real gameplay

Benny must swim through the actual 3D environment.

His body should follow the water slope and banking, remain partly immersed and stay fully visible.

Water splashes, steering, collisions, camera motion and coin pickups must respond to his real position.

No flat moving backgrounds, camera-following scenery pictures, missing geometry or distorted image textures.

4. Build one continuous connected world

The playable sequence is:

04 → Bubble Dash → Sock Rescue → 05 → 06 → 07 → 08 → 09 → 10.

Make the exit of each area physically meet the entrance of the next.

I noticed you found that the main game's world units are approximately three times larger than parts of the newer scenes. Please reconcile the scale of Benny, tunnels, river widths, camera and collision geometry.

Avoid sudden page loads, teleports, camera jumps and visual discontinuities.

5. Use the debugging tools we restored

Use Three.js DevTools and Spector.js to diagnose actual rendering problems.

Use Playwright to test real left/right swipes, forward swimming, jumping, coins and transitions.

Test the scenery with plain materials first to reveal missing geometry. Then restore my approved artwork textures.

Compare the beginning, middle and end of each playable section—not only the approved starting camera.

6. Preserve everything already working

Do not restart the game or rebuild completed sections unnecessarily.

Keep the successful Screen 06 water immersion, movement, camera and scenery improvements.

Preserve all approved images, Google Flow video scenes, working controls and GitHub backups.

Use my original approved screens as the visual targets. The newer preview images are guides for the transitions only, unless I explicitly approve a redesigned screen.

Keep saving successful progress to GitHub every five minutes.

My main goal is a beautiful, coherent, real 3D mobile game where Benny naturally swims through my original approved Rainbow scenery. Blender builds the world, Three.js makes it playable, and World Labs Atlas is only an optional helper when appropriate.

Please continue building and testing the connected game using this approach.

1	"""Rainbow screen kit - Blender component library (round 43, Blender 5.3 headless). Builds a screen's connected 3D scenery from its
2	fitted layout (tools/screenkit/screens/NN/fitNN.py -> layout.json) and exports ONE GLB with clean per-mesh UVs (0..1) for the
3	picture bake and the code materials. Reusable Geometry Nodes groups (created once per file, applied to curves the layout defines):
4	  RB_Sweep_Tube    circle profile swept along a curve, normals facing INSIDE (washer drums / tubes); radius per point = curve radius
5	  RB_Sweep_Ribbon  flat ribbon (water channel surface) swept along a curve, banked by the curve tilt, width = curve radius * 2
6	  RB_Sweep_Flume   the channel body under a ribbon: two rounded side lips + underside (the painted rainbow edges of a water slide)
7	  RB_Sweep_Band    rounded rectangular band profile swept around a circle (gold rings / collars hugging a drum wall)
8	  RB_FoamBank      points along a curve, jittered, instanced lumpy flattened ico spheres (foam heaps along banks)
9	Every sweep stores the UV map 'UVMap' (u = across the profile 0..1, v = along the curve 0..1) as a FLOAT2 face-corner attribute,
10	which glTF exports as TEXCOORD_0. Object names carry the material family the game assigns (tunnel_*, ring_*, water_*, pool_*,
11	flume_*, foam_*, paddle_*). Screen-specific numbers live ONLY in layout.json; this file has none.
12	  blender -b --python tools/screenkit/blender_kit.py -- <layout.json> <out.glb>
13	"""
14	import bpy, bmesh, sys, json, math
15	from mathutils import Vector
16	argv = sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--') + 1:]; LAY = json.load(open(argv[0])); OUT = argv[1]
17	bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
18	B2 = lambda p: Vector((p[0], -p[2], p[1]))            # game (x, y up, z) -> Blender (x, -z, y up)
19	
20	
21	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- node groups
22	def _link(ng, a, b): ng.links.new(a, b)
23	
24	
25	def sweep_group(name, profile, flip=False):
26	    """profile(ng) -> (profile geometry socket). Builds: curve -> capture v (spline factor) ; profile -> capture u ; Curve to Mesh with
27	    Scale = curve radius ; UVMap = (u, v) ; optional flip ; smooth shading."""
28	    if name in bpy.data.node_groups: return bpy.data.node_groups[name]
29	    ng = bpy.data.node_groups.new(name, 'GeometryNodeTree')
30	    ng.interface.new_socket('Geometry', in_out='INPUT', socket_type='NodeSocketGeometry')
31	    ng.interface.new_socket('Geometry', in_out='OUTPUT', socket_type='NodeSocketGeometry')
32	    N = ng.nodes; gin = N.new('NodeGroupInput'); gout = N.new('NodeGroupOutput')
33	    sp = N.new('GeometryNodeSplineParameter')
34	    capC = N.new('GeometryNodeCaptureAttribute'); capC.capture_items.new('FLOAT', 'v'); capC.domain = 'POINT'
35	    _link(ng, gin.outputs[0], capC.inputs['Geometry']); _link(ng, sp.outputs['Factor'], capC.inputs['v'])   # by name: Blender 5 has a Selection socket at index 1
36	    prof = profile(ng)
37	    sp2 = N.new('GeometryNodeSplineParameter')
38	    capP = N.new('GeometryNodeCaptureAttribute'); capP.capture_items.new('FLOAT', 'u'); capP.domain = 'POINT'
39	    _link(ng, prof, capP.inputs['Geometry']); _link(ng, sp2.outputs['Factor'], capP.inputs['u'])
40	    rad = N.new('GeometryNodeInputRadius')
41	    c2m = N.new('GeometryNodeCurveToMesh'); _link(ng, capC.outputs['Geometry'], c2m.inputs['Curve']); _link(ng, capP.outputs['Geometry'], c2m.inputs['Profile Curve'])
42	    _link(ng, rad.outputs[0], c2m.inputs['Scale'])
43	    comb = N.new('ShaderNodeCombineXYZ'); _link(ng, capP.outputs['u'], comb.inputs[0]); _link(ng, capC.outputs['v'], comb.inputs[1])
44	    st = N.new('GeometryNodeStoreNamedAttribute'); st.data_type = 'FLOAT2'; st.domain = 'CORNER'; st.inputs['Name'].default_value = 'UVMap'
45	    _link(ng, c2m.outputs[0], st.inputs['Geometry']); _link(ng, comb.outputs[0], st.inputs['Value'])
46	    last = st.outputs[0]
47	    if flip:
48	        ff = N.new('GeometryNodeFlipFaces'); _link(ng, last, ff.inputs[0]); last = ff.outputs[0]
49	    sm = N.new('GeometryNodeSetShadeSmooth'); _link(ng, last, sm.inputs[0]); _link(ng, sm.outputs[0], gout.inputs[0])

53	def prof_circle(res):
54	    def f(ng):
55	        # an OPEN full arc (first and last point coincide): the UV seam gets u = 0 and u = 1 at the same place instead of one face
56	        # wrapping backwards across the whole texture (a cyclic circle's closing face would)
57	        c = ng.nodes.new('GeometryNodeCurveArc'); c.inputs['Resolution'].default_value = res; c.inputs['Radius'].default_value = 1.0
