63	    """sweep group whose profile is an existing poly curve object (named name + '_prof'), referenced through an Object Info node"""
64	    if name in bpy.data.node_groups: return bpy.data.node_groups[name]

"""Rainbow screen kit - Blender component library (round 43, Blender 5.3 headless). Builds a screen's connected 3D scenery from its
fitted layout (tools/screenkit/screens/NN/fitNN.py -> layout.json) and exports ONE GLB with clean per-mesh UVs (0..1) for the
picture bake and the code materials. Reusable Geometry Nodes groups (created once per file, applied to curves the layout defines):
  RB_Sweep_Tube    circle profile swept along a curve, normals facing INSIDE (washer drums / tubes); radius per point = curve radius
  RB_Sweep_Ribbon  flat ribbon (water channel surface) swept along a curve, banked by the curve tilt, width = curve radius * 2
  RB_Sweep_Flume   the channel body under a ribbon: two rounded side lips + underside (the painted rainbow edges of a water slide)
  RB_Sweep_Band    rounded rectangular band profile swept around a circle (gold rings / collars hugging a drum wall)
  RB_FoamBank      points along a curve, jittered, instanced lumpy flattened ico spheres (foam heaps along banks)
Every sweep stores the UV map 'UVMap' (u = across the profile 0..1, v = along the curve 0..1) as a FLOAT2 face-corner attribute,
which glTF exports as TEXCOORD_0. Object names carry the material family the game assigns (tunnel_*, ring_*, water_*, pool_*,
flume_*, foam_*, paddle_*). Screen-specific numbers live ONLY in layout.json; this file has none.
  blender -b --python tools/screenkit/blender_kit.py -- <layout.json> <out.glb>
"""
import bpy, bmesh, sys, json, math
from mathutils import Vector
argv = sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--') + 1:]; LAY = json.load(open(argv[0])); OUT = argv[1]
bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
B2 = lambda p: Vector((p[0], -p[2], p[1]))            # game (x, y up, z) -> Blender (x, -z, y up)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- node groups
def _link(ng, a, b): ng.links.new(a, b)


def sweep_group(name, profile, flip=False):
    """profile(ng) -> (profile geometry socket). Builds: curve -> capture v (spline factor) ; profile -> capture u ; Curve to Mesh with
    Scale = curve radius ; UVMap = (u, v) ; optional flip ; smooth shading."""
    if name in bpy.data.node_groups: return bpy.data.node_groups[name]
    ng = bpy.data.node_groups.new(name, 'GeometryNodeTree')
    ng.interface.new_socket('Geometry', in_out='INPUT', socket_type='NodeSocketGeometry')
    ng.interface.new_socket('Geometry', in_out='OUTPUT', socket_type='NodeSocketGeometry')
    N = ng.nodes; gin = N.new('NodeGroupInput'); gout = N.new('NodeGroupOutput')
    sp = N.new('GeometryNodeSplineParameter')
    capC = N.new('GeometryNodeCaptureAttribute'); capC.capture_items.new('FLOAT', 'v'); capC.domain = 'POINT'
    _link(ng, gin.outputs[0], capC.inputs['Geometry']); _link(ng, sp.outputs['Factor'], capC.inputs['v'])   # by name: Blender 5 has a Selection socket at index 1
    prof = profile(ng)
    sp2 = N.new('GeometryNodeSplineParameter')
    capP = N.new('GeometryNodeCaptureAttribute'); capP.capture_items.new('FLOAT', 'u'); capP.domain = 'POINT'
    _link(ng, prof, capP.inputs['Geometry']); _link(ng, sp2.outputs['Factor'], capP.inputs['u'])
    rad = N.new('GeometryNodeInputRadius')
    c2m = N.new('GeometryNodeCurveToMesh'); _link(ng, capC.outputs['Geometry'], c2m.inputs['Curve']); _link(ng, capP.outputs['Geometry'], c2m.inputs['Profile Curve'])
    _link(ng, rad.outputs[0], c2m.inputs['Scale'])
    comb = N.new('ShaderNodeCombineXYZ'); _link(ng, capP.outputs['u'], comb.inputs[0]); _link(ng, capC.outputs['v'], comb.inputs[1])
    st = N.new('GeometryNodeStoreNamedAttribute'); st.data_type = 'FLOAT2'; st.domain = 'CORNER'; st.inputs['Name'].default_value = 'UVMap'
    _link(ng, c2m.outputs[0], st.inputs['Geometry']); _link(ng, comb.outputs[0], st.inputs['Value'])
    last = st.outputs[0]
    if flip:
        ff = N.new('GeometryNodeFlipFaces'); _link(ng, last, ff.inputs[0]); last = ff.outputs[0]
    sm = N.new('GeometryNodeSetShadeSmooth'); _link(ng, last, sm.inputs[0]); _link(ng, sm.outputs[0], gout.inputs[0])
    return ng


def prof_circle(res):
    def f(ng):
        # an OPEN full arc (first and last point coincide): the UV seam gets u = 0 and u = 1 at the same place instead of one face
        # wrapping backwards across the whole texture (a cyclic circle's closing face would)
        c = ng.nodes.new('GeometryNodeCurveArc'); c.inputs['Resolution'].default_value = res; c.inputs['Radius'].default_value = 1.0
        c.inputs['Start Angle'].default_value = 0.0; c.inputs['Sweep Angle'].default_value = 2 * math.pi; return c.outputs['Curve']
    return f


def object_profile_group(name, pts, flip=False):
    """sweep group whose profile is an existing poly curve object (named name + '_prof'), referenced through an Object Info node"""
    if name in bpy.data.node_groups: return bpy.data.node_groups[name]
    cu = bpy.data.curves.new(name + '_prof', 'CURVE'); cu.dimensions = '3D'; spl = cu.splines.new('POLY'); spl.points.add(len(pts) - 1)
    # pts are (across, up). Measured in Blender 5.3 (Z_UP twist): profile X -> the curve's right side, profile Y -> DOWN (so y is negated)
    for i, (x, y) in enumerate(pts): spl.points[i].co = (x, -y, 0, 1)   # measured: profile X -> sideways (right), profile -Y -> up
    pob = bpy.data.objects.new(name + '_prof', cu)                     # not linked to the scene: only referenced by the node group
    def f(ng):
        oi = ng.nodes.new('GeometryNodeObjectInfo'); oi.inputs['Object'].default_value = pob; return oi.outputs['Geometry']
    return sweep_group(name, f, flip)


def foam_group():
    name = 'RB_FoamBank'
    if name in bpy.data.node_groups: return bpy.data.node_groups[name]
    ng = bpy.data.node_groups.new(name, 'GeometryNodeTree'); N = ng.nodes
    ng.interface.new_socket('Geometry', in_out='INPUT', socket_type='NodeSocketGeometry')
    ng.interface.new_socket('Spacing', in_out='INPUT', socket_type='NodeSocketFloat')
    ng.interface.new_socket('Size', in_out='INPUT', socket_type='NodeSocketFloat')
    ng.interface.new_socket('Seed', in_out='INPUT', socket_type='NodeSocketInt')
    ng.interface.new_socket('Geometry', in_out='OUTPUT', socket_type='NodeSocketGeometry')
    gin = N.new('NodeGroupInput'); gout = N.new('NodeGroupOutput')
    rs = N.new('GeometryNodeResampleCurve'); rs.inputs['Mode'].default_value = 'Length'; _link(ng, gin.outputs[0], rs.inputs['Curve']); _link(ng, gin.outputs[1], rs.inputs['Length'])
    c2p = N.new('GeometryNodeCurveToPoints'); c2p.mode = 'EVALUATED'; _link(ng, rs.outputs[0], c2p.inputs['Curve'])
    jit = N.new('FunctionNodeRandomValue'); jit.data_type = 'FLOAT_VECTOR'; jit.inputs['Min'].default_value = (-1, -1, -0.15); jit.inputs['Max'].default_value = (1, 1, 0.1)
    _link(ng, gin.outputs[3], jit.inputs['Seed'])
    jsc = N.new('ShaderNodeVectorMath'); jsc.operation = 'SCALE'; _link(ng, jit.outputs['Value'], jsc.inputs[0]); _link(ng, gin.outputs[2], jsc.inputs['Scale'])
    sp = N.new('GeometryNodeSetPosition'); _link(ng, c2p.outputs['Points'], sp.inputs['Geometry']); _link(ng, jsc.outputs[0], sp.inputs['Offset'])
    ico = N.new('GeometryNodeMeshIcoSphere'); ico.inputs['Radius'].default_value = 1.0; ico.inputs['Subdivisions'].default_value = 2
    rnd = N.new('FunctionNodeRandomValue'); rnd.data_type = 'FLOAT'; rnd.inputs['Min'].default_value = 0.55; rnd.inputs['Max'].default_value = 1.25
    _link(ng, gin.outputs[3], rnd.inputs['Seed'])
    msz = N.new('ShaderNodeMath'); msz.operation = 'MULTIPLY'; _link(ng, rnd.outputs['Value'], msz.inputs[0]); _link(ng, gin.outputs[2], msz.inputs[1])
    flat = N.new('ShaderNodeCombineXYZ'); _link(ng, msz.outputs[0], flat.inputs[0]); _link(ng, msz.outputs[0], flat.inputs[1])
    mz = N.new('ShaderNodeMath'); mz.operation = 'MULTIPLY'; mz.inputs[1].default_value = 0.62; _link(ng, msz.outputs[0], mz.inputs[0]); _link(ng, mz.outputs[0], flat.inputs[2])
    iop = N.new('GeometryNodeInstanceOnPoints'); _link(ng, sp.outputs[0], iop.inputs['Points']); _link(ng, ico.outputs['Mesh'], iop.inputs['Instance']); _link(ng, flat.outputs[0], iop.inputs['Scale'])
    real = N.new('GeometryNodeRealizeInstances'); _link(ng, iop.outputs[0], real.inputs[0])
    sm = N.new('GeometryNodeSetShadeSmooth'); _link(ng, real.outputs[0], sm.inputs[0]); _link(ng, sm.outputs[0], gout.inputs[0])
    return ng


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- builders
def curve_object(name, pts, radii=None, tilts=None, cyclic=False, twist='Z_UP'):
    cu = bpy.data.curves.new(name + '_curve', 'CURVE'); cu.dimensions = '3D'; cu.twist_mode = twist
    spl = cu.splines.new('POLY'); spl.points.add(len(pts) - 1); spl.use_cyclic_u = cyclic
    for i, p in enumerate(pts):
        spl.points[i].co = (*B2(p), 1.0); spl.points[i].radius = radii[i] if radii else 1.0; spl.points[i].tilt = tilts[i] if tilts else 0.0
    ob = bpy.data.objects.new(name, cu); bpy.context.collection.objects.link(ob); return ob


def apply_group(ob, ng, inputs=None):
    mod = ob.modifiers.new('kit', 'NODES'); mod.node_group = ng
    for k, v in (inputs or {}).items():
        sock = next(s for s in ng.interface.items_tree if getattr(s, 'in_out', '') == 'INPUT' and s.name == k); sock.default_value = v   # Blender 5: set the group default, applied at once below
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = ob
    for o in bpy.context.selected_objects: o.select_set(False)
    ob.select_set(True); bpy.ops.object.convert(target='MESH'); return bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active


def grid(name, nu, nv, fn, flip=False):

  else if (fam === 'arrow') m = new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({ color: new THREE.Color(0.86, 0.98, 1.0), toneMapped: false });   // game-drawn white arrows (masked out of the bake, like the coins)

new="""  const all = []; world.traverse((o) => { if (o.isMesh && o.name !== 'drum_end' && o.userData.fam !== 'foam' && o.userData.fam !== 'arrow') all.push(o); });"""
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new)
old="""copper: [0.7, 0.6, 0.55], foam: [0.9, 0.9, 0.92] };"""
new="""copper: [0.7, 0.6, 0.55], foam: [0.9, 0.9, 0.92], funnel: [0.52, 0.64, 0.74], wall: [0.66, 0.6, 0.66], arrow: [0.95, 0.95, 0.95] };"""
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s); print('patched')
EOF

import json, struct
def meshes(path):
    b=open(path,'rb').read(); n=struct.unpack('<I',b[12:16])[0]; J=json.loads(b[20:20+n])
    out=[]
    for nd in J['nodes']:
        if 'mesh' not in nd: continue
        m=J['meshes'][nd['mesh']]; mn=[1e9]*3; mx=[-1e9]*3
        for p in m['primitives']:
            a=J['accessors'][p['attributes']['POSITION']]; mn=[min(x,y) for x,y in zip(mn,a['min'])]; mx=[max(x,y) for x,y in zip(mx,a['max'])]
        t=nd.get('translation',[0,0,0]); out.append((nd.get('name'),[round(x+tt,2) for x,tt in zip(mn,t)],[round(x+tt,2) for x,tt in zip(mx,t)]))
    return out
M=meshes('public/section/section.glb')
print(len(M),'meshes'); 
near=[m for m in M if m[2][2]>-3.0]
for m in sorted(near,key=lambda m:-m[2][2])[:30]: print(m)
EOF

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Rainbow screen kit: put a kit-built screen INTO the Rainbow app build (public/screenNN/ -> dist -> the Android APK).
#   bash tools/screenkit/build_screen_app.sh <NN> <workspace made by setup_screen.sh>
# Self-contained static scene (three.js 0.180 vendored, no CDN), textures pre-baked once (screen_export.cjs); the approved picture itself is
# NOT shipped (only the baked textures). The game hands over to it only in a test build (Screen 06: VITE_RAINBOW_KIT06=1 or ?kit06=1).
set -e
NN=${1:?screen}; SRC=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd); WS=$(cd "${2:?workspace}" && pwd); G="$WS/game"; P="$SRC/public/screen$NN"
rm -rf "$WS/app"; NODE_PATH=$(npm root -g) node "$SRC/tools/screenkit/screen_export.cjs" "$G" "$WS/app"
rm -rf "$P"; mkdir -p "$P/vendor/three/build" "$P/vendor/three/examples/jsm/loaders" "$P/vendor/three/examples/jsm/utils" "$P/baked"
T=/tmp/rainbow_r34/node_modules/three
cp "$T/build/three.module.js" "$T/build/three.core.js" "$P/vendor/three/build/"; cp "$T/examples/jsm/loaders/GLTFLoader.js" "$P/vendor/three/examples/jsm/loaders/"; cp "$T/examples/jsm/utils/BufferGeometryUtils.js" "$P/vendor/three/examples/jsm/utils/"
cp "$WS/app/baked/"* "$P/baked/"
for f in scene.glb layout.json controls.js swimfx.js benny31.glb bake.png coin.png splash.png bubble.png glint.png; do cp -L "$G/$f" "$P/$f"; done
python3 - "$SRC/tools/screenkit/screen.html" "$P/index.html" <<'PY'
import sys
s = open(sys.argv[1]).read()
a = '"three":"./node_modules/three/build/three.module.js","three/addons/":"./node_modules/three/examples/jsm/"'
assert a in s; s = s.replace(a, '"three":"./vendor/three/build/three.module.js","three/addons/":"./vendor/three/examples/jsm/"')
a = "const q = new URLSearchParams(location.search);"; assert a in s
s = s.replace(a, a + "\nif (!q.has('w') && !q.has('play')) q.set('play', '1');   // app: real-time play\nif (!q.has('prebaked')) q.set('prebaked', '1');   // app: textures baked offline")
open(sys.argv[2], 'w').write(s)
PY
du -sh "$P" | cut -f1 | xargs echo "screen $NN in the app build:" "$P"

"""Rainbow ONE connected world (round 44) - layout step. Places the areas in ONE coordinate system so each area's exit physically meets the next
area's entrance, assembles ONE route (Benny's path) through all of them, the camera keys (each area's fitted picture cameras, exact there),
the coins, and the Blender connector pieces (tools/world/blender_connectors.py).
  python3 -I tools/world/world_layout.py <04 kit layout.json> <section.json> <out dir>
Area order of play (user, 2026-11-22): 04 -> A Bubble Dash -> B Sock Rescue (A + B = the section) -> 05 -> 06 -> 07 -> 08 -> 09 -> 10.
v1 = 04 -> A -> B. Units: the kit / section units (water under Benny y = 0, camera 0.734 above it at each picture). Benny measures 0.473 u in 04
and 0.468 u in the section (1 % apart: one physical Benny, no rescaling needed for these two). The old game's units are ~3x larger; areas
that come from it are rebuilt with the kit in these units (user decision r44) - nothing is scaled at run time.
Join 04 -> A: 04's gold tube ends in a round doorway in the Bubble Dash chamber's near wall (the chamber is open behind its picture camera:
side walls / ceiling / floor run to z = +2 in section coordinates, nothing closes them). Both waters at y = 0; the route runs straight on.
"""
import sys, os, json, math
import numpy as np

L04 = json.load(open(sys.argv[1])); SEC = json.load(open(sys.argv[2])); OUT = sys.argv[3]; os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
DS = 0.05


def resample(P, step=DS):
    P = np.asarray(P, float); L = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(np.linalg.norm(np.diff(P, axis=0), axis=1))])
    s = np.arange(0, L[-1] + 1e-9, step); return np.stack([np.interp(s, L, P[:, i]) for i in range(3)], 1)


# ---- area 04 (kit): its own coordinates are the world's (offset 0)
D4 = L04['drum']; R4 = D4['r']; r4 = np.array(L04['route']['points']); z_end4 = float(r4[-1][2])
assert D4.get('open_end'), '04 must be built with --open-end (its tube stops at the doorway)'
# ---- area AB (section): its near wall plane (z = +2 in section coordinates) = 04's tube end; its route start continues 04's route
RT = SEC['route']; z0s = -RT['z0']; xs = np.array(RT['x'])
def RX(z): x = min(max((-z - RT['z0']) / RT['ds'], 0), len(xs) - 1.001); i = int(x); f = x - i; return xs[i] + (xs[i + 1] - xs[i]) * f
Z_NEAR_SEC = SEC['chamber']['z_near']                       # 2.0: where the chamber's side walls / ceiling / floor end behind its camera
T = np.array([float(r4[-1][0]) - RX(z0s), 0.0, z_end4 - Z_NEAR_SEC])   # route x continuous at the section's route start; near wall at 04's end
# section route points (world), from its first point to the level end inside the Sock Rescue tunnel
ZB0 = SEC['benny']['bubble'][2]; z_lev = SEC['tunnel'].get('z_level_end', SEC['tunnel']['z_exit'] - 4.5)
zz = np.arange(z0s, z_lev - 1e-9, -DS); rs = np.stack([[RX(z) for z in zz], np.zeros_like(zz), zz], 1) + T
# ---- connector route 04 end -> section start (the doorway): C1 Hermite, both ends heading -z
p0, p1 = r4[-1], rs[0]; n = max(8, int(np.linalg.norm(p1 - p0) / DS))
tt = np.linspace(0, 1, n + 1)[1:-1]; Ldist = float(np.linalg.norm(p1 - p0))
h00 = 2 * tt ** 3 - 3 * tt ** 2 + 1; h10 = tt ** 3 - 2 * tt ** 2 + tt; h01 = -2 * tt ** 3 + 3 * tt ** 2; h11 = tt ** 3 - tt ** 2
m0 = m1 = np.array([0, 0, -Ldist])
rc = h00[:, None] * p0 + h10[:, None] * m0 + h01[:, None] * p1 + h11[:, None] * m1
route = resample(np.vstack([r4, rc, rs]))
bank = np.zeros(len(route))
def s_of(P): return float(np.argmin(np.linalg.norm(route - np.asarray(P), axis=1)) * DS)
s04_end = s_of(r4[-1]); sAB0 = s_of(rs[0]); s_bub = s_of(np.array(SEC['benny']['bubble']) + T); s_sock = s_of(np.array(SEC['benny']['sock']) + T)
LEVEL = float((len(route) - 1) * DS)
# ---- camera keys: Benny's route position at each approved picture + that picture's fitted camera (world). Exact there; blended between.
c4 = L04['cams'][0]; ahead4 = L04['benny'].get('ahead', 0.0)
keys = [{'area': '04', 's': float(c4['s_ref'] + ahead4), 'pos': c4['pos'], 'yaw': c4['yaw'], 'pitch': c4['pitch'], 'ref': c4['ref']}]
for nm, sb in (('bubble', s_bub), ('sock', s_sock)):
    c = SEC['cams'][nm]; keys.append({'area': 'AB', 's': sb, 'pos': (np.array(c['pos']) + T).tolist(), 'yaw': c['yaw'], 'pitch': c['pitch'], 'ref': c['ref']})
# ---- areas: s ranges, titles (each picture's own HUD title), camera clamp (the camera never leaves the tube / chamber)
areas = [
    {'id': '04', 'kind': 'kit', 'dir': 'a04/', 'offset': [0, 0, 0], 's0': 0.0, 's1': s04_end, 'title': '04 · THROUGH THE FIVE ARROWS', 'coins_start': L04.get('coins_start', 1330),
     'clamp': {'type': 'tube', 'axis': [D4['axis_x'], D4['axis_y']], 'r': R4, 'z0': D4['z0'] + 0.5, 'z1': z_end4}},
    {'id': 'AB', 'kind': 'section', 'dir': 'aAB/', 'offset': T.tolist(), 's0': s04_end, 's1': LEVEL,
     'titles': [[s04_end, 'BUBBLE DASH CHAMBER'], [s_bub + (s_sock - s_bub) * 0.62, 'SOCK RESCUE TUNNEL']], 'mission_from': s_bub + (s_sock - s_bub) * 0.62},
]
# ---- connector pieces (Blender): the chamber's near wall with the doorway of 04's tube + a gold collar ring around it
CH = SEC['chamber']
conn = [{'name': 'cwall_04A', 'kind': 'wall_hole', 'z': z_end4, 'x0': CH['xl'] + T[0], 'x1': CH['xr'] + T[0], 'y0': -0.4, 'y1': CH['yc'],
         'hole': [D4['axis_x'], D4['axis_y'], R4], 'area': 'AB', 'fam': 'pink'},
        {'name': 'cring_04A', 'kind': 'collar', 'z': z_end4 + 0.06, 'axis': [D4['axis_x'], D4['axis_y']], 'r': R4 + 0.02, 'band': 0.3, 'area': '04', 'fam': 'ring'},
        {'name': 'cwater_04A', 'kind': 'strip', 'z0': z_end4 + 0.6, 'z1': z_end4 - 1.2, 'x0': D4['axis_x'] - R4, 'x1': D4['axis_x'] + R4, 'y': -0.01, 'area': '04', 'fam': 'pool'}]
world = {'version': 1, 'note': 'round 44: 04 -> A Bubble Dash -> B Sock Rescue in ONE scene (tools/world/world.html)', 'ds': DS, 'LEVEL': LEVEL,
         'route': {'points': route.round(5).tolist(), 'bank': bank.tolist()}, 'areas': areas, 'cam_keys': keys, 'connectors': conn,
         'joins': [{'from': '04', 'to': 'A', 's': s04_end, 'kind': 'doorway', 'z': z_end4}],
         'start_s': keys[0]['s'], 'benny_h': L04['benny']['height']}
json.dump(world, open(os.path.join(OUT, 'world.json'), 'w'))
json.dump({'connectors': conn}, open(os.path.join(OUT, 'connectors_spec.json'), 'w'), indent=1)
print(f"04 tube end z {z_end4:.2f}; section offset {T.round(3).tolist()}; route {LEVEL:.2f} u (04 0-{s04_end:.2f}, AB {s04_end:.2f}-{LEVEL:.2f}); "
      f"picture keys s: 04 {keys[0]['s']:.2f}, Bubble Dash {s_bub:.2f}, Sock Rescue {s_sock:.2f}")

tools/world/world_layout.py -> connectors_spec.json, exported as ONE GLB with clean per-mesh UVs (the world page gives each piece the material
family of the area it belongs to, so it matches that area's look). Kinds:
  wall_hole  a flat wall (x0..x1, y0..y1 at z) with a round doorway (hole cx, cy, r): a polar grid from the hole rim out to the rectangle
  collar     a gold band ring around a doorway (the kit's RB_Sweep_Band profile)
  strip      a flat water strip (x0..x1 at height y, from z0 to z1) that closes any gap between two areas' water surfaces
  blender -b --python tools/world/blender_connectors.py -- <connectors_spec.json> <out.glb>
"""
import bpy, bmesh, sys, json, math
from mathutils import Vector
argv = sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--') + 1:]; SPEC = json.load(open(argv[0])); OUT = argv[1]
bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
B2 = lambda p: Vector((p[0], -p[2], p[1]))            # game (x, y up, z) -> Blender (x, -z, y up)


def grid(name, nu, nv, fn, flip=False):
    me = bpy.data.meshes.new(name); bm = bmesh.new(); uvl = bm.loops.layers.uv.new('UVMap'); V, UV = [], []
    for j in range(nv + 1):
        row, ru = [], []
        for i in range(nu + 1):
            p, uv = fn(i / nu, j / nv); row.append(bm.verts.new(B2(p))); ru.append(uv)
        V.append(row); UV.append(ru)
    for j in range(nv):
        for i in range(nu):
            q = [V[j][i], V[j][i + 1], V[j + 1][i + 1], V[j + 1][i]]; uq = [UV[j][i], UV[j][i + 1], UV[j + 1][i + 1], UV[j + 1][i]]

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Rainbow ONE connected world (round 44): build the playable world folder 04 -> A Bubble Dash -> B Sock Rescue (more areas join as they are
# rebuilt with the screen kit). Free tools only (Blender 5.3, three.js, the kit); no credits.
#   bash tools/world/setup_world.sh <workspace>      -> <workspace>/game/play3.html (= tools/world/world.html), QA as any kit page
# Steps: 04 with the kit (tunnel ending in the doorway: --tube-len 22 --open-end) -> its bake once offline (screen_export.cjs) ->
# the section's pre-baked folder (public/section, unchanged) -> world_layout.py (placements, ONE route, camera keys, connectors) ->
# Blender connector pieces (blender_connectors.py) -> game folder.
set -e
SRC=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd); WS=${1:?workspace}; mkdir -p "$WS"; WS=$(cd "$WS" && pwd); G="$WS/game"
bash "$SRC/tools/screenkit/setup_screen.sh" 04 "$WS/s04" > "$WS/s04.log" 2>&1
bash "$SRC/tools/screenkit/variant.sh" 04 "$WS/s04" "$WS/w04" --tube-len 22 --open-end > /dev/null
NODE_PATH=$(npm root -g) node "$SRC/tools/screenkit/screen_export.cjs" "$WS/w04/game" "$WS/w04/app" > "$WS/w04_export.log" 2>&1
rm -rf "$G"; mkdir -p "$G/a04/baked" "$G/aAB"
cp "$WS/w04/game/layout.json" "$WS/w04/game/scene.glb" "$G/a04/"; cp "$WS/w04/app/baked/"* "$G/a04/baked/"
cp -r "$SRC/public/section/baked" "$G/aAB/"; cp "$SRC/public/section/section.json" "$SRC/public/section/section.glb" "$G/aAB/"
python3 -I "$SRC/tools/world/world_layout.py" "$G/a04/layout.json" "$G/aAB/section.json" "$G" | tee "$WS/world_layout.log"
blender -b --python "$SRC/tools/world/blender_connectors.py" -- "$G/connectors_spec.json" "$G/connectors.glb" > "$WS/connectors.log" 2>&1 || { tail -20 "$WS/connectors.log"; exit 1; }
cp "$SRC/tools/world/world.html" "$G/play3.html"; cp "$SRC/tools/kit05/controls.js" "$SRC/tools/kit05/swimfx.js" "$G/"
for f in benny31.glb bake.png coin.png splash.png bubble.png glint.png; do cp -L "$WS/w04/game/$f" "$G/$f"; done
ln -sfn /tmp/rainbow_r34/node_modules "$G/node_modules"
echo "world ready: $G/play3.html"

"""Screen 05 'Flow Into the Current' - FIT step of the screen kit (round 44, for the one connected world). Measures the user's approved picture
references/05_flow_into_the_current.png (read-only) and writes ONE physical world for it (<out>/layout.json + fit overlay).
  python3 -I tools/screenkit/screens/05/fit05.py <out dir> [--set key=json] [--tube-len L] [--open-end]
Measured on the picture (864 x 1536 px, gridded crops qa/world/r44/05/measure):
  * the bright tunnel core (vanishing point) at (500, 474); the big gold ring (top (440, 205), sides at the frame edges): circle (437, 560) r 420
    -> camera offset from the tube axis = ((500-437)/420, (560-474)/420) radii (right, up); the inner rings agree within the painting's slack.
  * the water line at that ring: the foam banks meet the wall at y ~ 700 on both sides -> the axis is (700-560)/420 radii above the water;
    with the camera 0.734 above the water this fixes the tube radius.
  * Benny: water contact (430, 1185), pompom top (430, 770). Coins (centre, radius): the painted S-trail. Copper trays (centre, width).
  * the river fills the tube floor (pink edges + cyan core, S-curves through the coins): the floor water is the tube's own pool; Benny's
    route = a smooth curve THROUGH his water point and every coin's water point (coins stay collectable), then straight on down the tube.
"""
import sys, os, json, math, argparse
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)); KIT = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(HERE, '..', '..')); REPO = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(KIT, '..', '..'))
sys.path.insert(0, KIT)
import fitlib as fl   # noqa: E402

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(); ap.add_argument('out'); ap.add_argument('--da2'); ap.add_argument('--set', action='append', default=[])
ap.add_argument('--tube-len', type=float, default=40.0); ap.add_argument('--open-end', action='store_true')
a = ap.parse_args(); os.makedirs(a.out, exist_ok=True)
REF = 'references/05_flow_into_the_current.png'; W, H = 864, 1536

content.text:
Your first priority stretch is now one connected world: **04 → Bubble Dash → Sock Rescue → 05**, in one scene with no page loads. It's recorded uninterrupted with real finger swipes, and nothing is finished yet.

**How the joins are built (Blender for the scenery, Three.js for play):**
- **04 → Bubble Dash:** I rebuilt Screen 04 with the screen kit. Its gold tunnel now ends in a real round doorway into the Bubble Dash chamber, with a gold collar. The water stays at one level and Benny keeps the same size.
- **Bubble Dash → Sock Rescue:** already one piece; the chamber's river runs through the gold arch into the tunnel.
- **Sock Rescue → 05:** I rebuilt Screen 05 with the kit. The narrow Sock Rescue tunnel curves sideways and widens into 05's current through a 9-unit connector tube with gold rings and continuous water.

**What the recordings show:**

| | 04 → Bubble Dash → Sock Rescue | Sock Rescue → 05 |
|---|---|---|
| Frames | 1,083 (gray and textured) | 574 (gray and textured) |
| Swipes recognised | 17 / 17 | 10 / 10 |
| Benny on screen | every frame | every frame |
| Hole pixels | 0 | 0 |
| Fastest camera turn | 0.67° per frame | 0.72° per frame |

In both, the scenery never moves and Benny stays on the real water.

The first Sock Rescue → 05 take had a hairline crack at the tube seam and a fast camera turn in 05's S-river. I fixed both and re-recorded; the table shows the second take.

**Your approved views survive the joins.** At each picture's own camera, the world measures the same as each level's own page: 04 83.8 %, Bubble Dash 87.4 %, Sock Rescue 81.3 %, 05 80.6 %. Separately, the app's saved textures cost 3–4 points compared with baking them live, which I still need to fix.

**Ratings, from my earlier message:**
- At each picture's own camera: 8–9 out of 10.
- While Benny swims: 4–7 out of 10. Away from what your painting's camera saw, the game shows simpler stand-in walls and water. That's the main gap to your 9/10 target.
- 07–10 aren't rebuilt yet: about 3 out of 10 while swimming.

**Not done yet:**
- 06 isn't in the world yet. It needs scaling to Benny's size here (its units are about 18 % larger) and the rising join into its banked crest.
- 07–10 aren't rebuilt; that includes the real descent from 07 into 08.
- The world isn't in the Android app yet; I'll rebuild the APK when you accept it.
- In the gray test Bubble Dash / Sock Rescue show orange because their surfaces face the other way. It's cosmetic and I'll flip them.

**Next:**
1. Bring 06 into the world.
2. Rebuild 07 and 08 with the real descent between them.
3. Raise the "while swimming" look by giving the stand-in walls, rings and water your paintings' own colours and detail.

Please watch the two textured recordings and tell me if the doorway and the curving tunnel feel right. Everything is saved to GitHub: commit `636a02ef`, the same commit on GitHub.
